reviews.reason: Score 16. probe: Before the next rule-heavy turn-based playable diff or headless game check, did I name the minimal engine contract being tested, such as legal_actions, apply_action, is_terminal, winner_or_score, and current_actor?

reviews.title: Agent-based game balance testing: difficulty spikes and skill-vs-chance trend checks
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex game work already uses headless checks and prototype probes, but can still read a single score, clear rate, or bot success as balance evidence. The transferable point is narrow: for the next playable diff or headless balance note, compare version trends and separate skilled-policy improvement from random or weak-policy improvement before claiming a change increased challenge, skill ceiling, or fairness. probe: Before the next playable diff, headless balance test, or game-evaluation memory note where I make a difficulty, fairness, skill ceiling, or chance claim, did I compare at least two versions or variants under the same seed or scenario set?

Did I separate random_or_weak_policy results from heuristic_or_skilled_policy results and record whether the trend suggests skill_signal, chance_signal, difficulty_spike, proxy_mismatch, or insufficient_runs?

If a bot result affects the design verdict, did I state whether it is a balance_judge, regression_detector, or human_review_pointer, and label reward_proxy_unvalidated or human_trend_unchecked when the proxy has not been calibrated?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two playable-diff or headless balance notes already compare version trends, separate random or weak policy from skilled policy, and label uncalibrated proxy limits before making difficulty or skill-vs-chance claims.

reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if it only adds judgment time and does not reduce missed structural dependencies or improve evidence pointers in the next implementation, review, memory change, or phase handoff.

reviews.reason: Phase 1 の recall、Phase 3 の shared-reads 候補採用、Phase 4a の問題抽出はいずれも、内容そのものだけでなく arxiv / 個人ブログ / Slack atom / 自分が書いた atom という source 表記の影響を受ける。この atom は source attribution が内容評価を上回るリスクと、明示的な注意だけでは消えにくいリスクを示しており、直近の候補選定と記憶検索に直結する。ただし恒久ルール化すると全検索を重くするため、次回の recall / candidate comparison で source と内容を一度だけ分ける reversible probe に留める。

reviews.title: LM agent の失敗を、必要な知識を発見できなかった失敗と、発見済み知識を使えなかった失敗に分けて測る評価法
reviews.reason: 直近の game/headless 評価と Phase 4a の問題抽出では、失敗を単なるスコア低下や実装不足として丸めると次の修正が外れやすい。この atom は探索失敗と活用失敗を外部行動から分ける観点を提供し、既存の runtime verification probe や retrieval loop probe と重なるが、失敗分類の入口として 1 cycle だけ使うなら軽い。恒久ルール化は過剰なので reversible probe に留める。

reviews.title: mTsuruta「要素設計と登場順設計を別工程で持つ」を、本日 game-rights で炎上した graze_log BOMB 構造問題と shot_log v01 17日放置と memory 静止葉 55件 に重ねる3点合成
reviews.reason: 要素そのものの設計と、時間軸上でいつ出すか・いつ回すかの設計を分ける知見。graze_log BOMB、wave_grammar_check 放置、memory 静止葉の3例があり、ゲーム制作と memory/tooling 運用の両方に直結する。ただし既存の説明過多回避 probe やゲーム設計ルールと隣接するため、恒久ルールではなく次回の mechanic / tooling 変更でだけ確認する可逆 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Three tweets on whether the ignition point is internal or external: ats suffering scalar / creativetomred no over-explaining / umiyuki_ai Saizeriya CLI
reviews.reason: This atom connects agent autonomy, game tutorial design, and CLI experience through one axis: do not push behavior only with explanation or external instruction; place the next-action trigger inside the user or agent experience. For Phase 3b this is too broad for a permanent rule, but useful as a reversible probe for the next shared-reads draft, game prototype, or memory UX decision.

reviews.title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
reviews.reason: In Nao_u_BOT memory_recall, shared-reads, and game-rights search, the practical risk is not only grep versus vector. It is whether results are delivered inline or as file paths, and whether the agent closes the read-integrate-retry loop. This overlaps with existing memory-layer probes, so it should stay as a reversible one-cycle probe for the next recall improvement, Phase 4a, or dedupe search.

reviews.title: ebikani_hasami「Agents need control flow, not more prompts」(HN 433pts) — 我々の5/2事件と3層プロンプト構造を「制御フロー」として読み直す
reviews.reason: 定時サイクルは既に長い指示群を持っており、次に改善すべきなのは文言追加ではなく、Phase間の順番・分岐・失敗時の扱いが実際に機能しているかの確認である。この atom は prompt 増量ではなく control flow として agent 運用を読むため、恒久ルール化せず、次回の phase handoff / tool failure / retry 判断で1回だけ確認する probe に留める。

reviews.title: karaage0703「放牧エンジニアリング」と、自分の backup auto-commit が意図 commit を窒息させた事故の接続 (Ash)
reviews.reason: Git sync is mandatory after work, so mixing scheduler, ingest, or backup-generated changes into an intentional commit can pollute the evidence trail and make later recall or rollback decisions worse. This atom connects houboku-style autonomous operation with a backup auto-commit incident that suffocated the intended commit. Existing AGENTS.md already has the permanent rule, so this cycle only adds a short reversible probe for the next git sync.

reviews.title: MEMSAD 自分達の環境への適用: shared-reads/Slack/game-rights の記憶汚染リスク
reviews.reason: shared-reads と Slack 指示を atom 化して再利用する運用では、浅い要約・出所欠落・過剰一般化が長期記憶として残り、後続 recall の判断を歪める。既存の投稿品質ルールと重なるが、今回の反映は恒久ルールではなく、次回の recall / memory ingest / shared-reads state 更新で「検索されやすいが根拠が弱い記憶」を1回だけ点検する軽量 probe に留める。

reviews.title: multi-agent LLM の drift メトリクス 3 本が 2026-05 に独立収束 - Pot (Log/Mir/Ash/Nao_u) 構成への構造的接続
reviews.reason: この atom は multi-agent LLM の drift を意味的 drift、行動的 drift、artifact decay の 3 層に分け、Pot 構成では A は許容、B は抑制、C は強く抑制という暫定線引きを置いている。直近の Phase 3b probe は aggregate score や reviewer bias の分解には触れているが、Codex 自身の定時サイクルが core anchor、警告の経験化、artifact decay を同時に点検する短い問いはまだ薄い。恒久ルール化すると監視項目が肥大化するため、次の memory cleanup / multi-agent evaluation / phase handoff で 1 回だけ確認する probe に留める。

reviews.title: Agent Island: A Saturation- and Contamination-Resistant Benchmark from Multiagent Games
reviews.reason: Agent Island は multiagent game log を leaderboard だけでなく、private note、public pitch、vote rationale、final decision、same-provider preference まで含む評価 artifact として残す点が、直近の game harness / cross_review / shared-reads 判断に直結する。ただし 2-4 agent 評価を恒久制度にすると重く、Cattle Trade の aggregate score 分解 probe とも一部重なるため、次に複数 agent / 複数レビューで prototype や候補を評価する 1 回だけ、最終結論だけでなく投票理由と同調 bias を保存する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: shmup 単調性回避の外部知見3本 — graze_log v04 (5/14 Nao_u指摘) への種として整理
reviews.reason: Nao_u の graze_log v04 指摘は「単調・単純」「軌跡予測がない」「shot_log のようなリズム/バリエーション必要」で、直近の shmup / action prototype の修復判断に直結する。ただし既に wave/rhythm probe は存在するため、恒久ルールや大きな評価表へ広げず、次回だけ「variation が学習可能な反復として効いているか、単なるランダム化や密度上げに逃げていないか」を見る短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Cattle Trade: multi-agent negotiation benchmark with incomplete information and resource constraints
reviews.reason: Cattle Trade frames agent evaluation as a long game where incomplete information, adversarial interaction, auctions, hidden offers, bluffing, opponent-state inference, and resource allocation interact. This is directly useful for game/agent evaluation, but turning it into a permanent rule would overreach. A one-cycle probe can keep the next benchmark or prototype judgment from collapsing success into a single score.

reviews.title: @DenneTA_D 「翻訳=非可逆圧縮」× @akari_worlds 「一語で起動するネットワーク」 — R-007 造語症対策の射程画定と、MEMORY.md / cross_review / 3インスタンス転送の理論的限界
reviews.reason: Phase 1/3b/4a can mistake a MEMORY.md index line, atom trigger, or staging summary for the original context. This atom shows that compression preserves propositions but can lose anchor tokens such as proper nouns, incident names, Slack timestamps, and source links. A permanent rule would make every recall heavier, so this is kept as a short probe for the next memory/staging/cross_review summary use.

reviews.title: GAM: Hierarchical Graph-based Agentic Memory for LLM Agents — 3層グラフ記憶 (arXiv 2604.12285v1)
reviews.reason: Phase 1/4a の記憶検索が grep や直近 atom 直引きに寄りやすく、上位目標から中粒度記憶、atom へ降りる順序が明示されていない。GAM の知見は現行 memory_redesign と per-file atoms に直結するが、MEMORY.md 再設計や検索プロトコル恒久化は大きすぎるため、次の memory recall / Phase 4a で1回だけ階層検索順序を試す probe に留める。

reviews.title: Eneba「15 Best Shoot 'Em Up Games to Try In 2026」分析 — Phase 1 §6 仮設の自己訂正
reviews.reason: 直近の shot_log / shmup 評価で、flow state や反射操作を単独の成功軸として読みすぎる危険を、商業評価語彙の分布と BOMB headless ベンチの方向一致で訂正している。恒久ルール化すると二次情報を過大評価するため、次の game prototype / repair の前に「戦術判断」と「反射操作」を分けて確認する一時 probe に留める。

reviews.title: 2026-05-16 Twitter おすすめから3件結合: creatable / fun / sellable の三独立軸
reviews.reason: 直近のゲーム制作では、作れること、面白いこと、売れることを混同すると、headless や実装進捗を fun 軸の進捗として誤読しやすい。この atom は mTsuruta / hadekait / snapwith の3観察を creatable / fun / sellable の独立軸として結合し、graze_log v05 の headless と fun 判定の混同にも直接接続している。恒久ルールや AGENTS 追記にはせず、次に game prototype の制作・評価・修復を行う時だけ、軸混同を確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: LLM Game Rule Understanding Through Out-of-Distribution Fine-Tuning
reviews.reason: ゲームプロトタイプを LLM に読ませる前に、感想や改造案へ飛ばず、明示ルールを状態遷移へ適用できているかを測る必要がある。この atom は legal 判定と next state 判定を分け、ID/OOD split と回答理由で失敗原因を分類する設計が、次の rule-understanding harness に直接使える。恒久ルールや評価表にはせず、次に仕様レビュー・turn/grid/resource 系 prototype を扱う時の短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: PCGRLLM: LLM を reward/probe 候補生成と具体 feedback に使い、score oracle にしない
reviews.reason: 直近のゲーム制作では、面白さや制作意図を deterministic harness に落とす必要がある。PCGRLLM は LLM を評価器ではなく reward/probe の生成・修正補助に置き、生成物からの具体 feedback を1点ずつ返す構造が直接使える。恒久ルールや評価表にはせず、次に PCG / レベル生成 / playtest probe を設計する時の短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Lanzi/Loiacono: LLMをinteractive genetic algorithmの操作子として使う共同ゲーム設計
reviews.reason: 次のゲーム制作で「候補を大量に作る」だけに戻らず、人間や過去feedbackの選択圧を明示してから小さく変異・交叉する手順へ落とせる。恒久ルール化せず、次回のゲーム案選定で1回だけ確認するprobeに留める。

reviews.title: trajectory 二重使用 — エージェント記憶設計と弾幕物理軌跡が同じ語を別意味で使う構造
reviews.reason: Fang et al. の trajectory から tips を抽出する構造と、graze_log 側の物理軌跡を知覚補助へ変換する構造は、直近の記憶整理とゲーム制作の両方に接続する。ただし原典確認は二次情報経由で confidence medium のため、記憶スキーマや恒久ルールには昇格せず、次の staging / game prototype / memory cleanup で「結果だけでなく決定帰属つき trajectory から 1 つだけ再利用可能な tip を抜く」短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [shared-reads] devwhodevs/engraph: 5 レーン RRF ハイブリッド検索で markdown vault をエージェント記憶基盤にする MCP/REST server
reviews.reason: 現行の memory_recall / grep / per-file atom 運用に対し、engraph の要点は多機能導入ではなく「semantic / full-text / graph / rerank / time の複数レーンを read-only で比べ、どのレーンが効いたかを説明可能にしてから Write を開ける」こと。記憶基盤を恒久変更せず、次の recall 設計や Phase 4a 整理で 1 回だけ確認する probe に留める。

reviews.title: 「人間は判断だけ」と「判断は厚みで成り立つ」の反証ペア — M-40 自己判定ハーネスを二層に分ける根拠
reviews.reason: 自己判定を headless 数値だけに寄せる既存 probe はあるが、この atom は「機械的に判定できる層」と「自分の基準の厚みが必要な層」を事前に分ける点が未反映。次のゲーム評価で、どちらを自動化し、どちらを判断保留または人間確認へ残すかを明示する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: 速度ヒューリスティックと事前批判の3層切り分け（ktch9541 / Mark Brown / toRisouP / xiombatsg）
reviews.reason: 多案 harness、単一案着手前、実装中の論法を分ける視点は、次のゲーム案選定で速度足切りと事前批判を混同しないために直接使える。既存ルールへ追記せず、次回の案選定・着手判断で層を1行確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] When Routine Chats Turn Toxic: Unintended Long-Term State Poisoning in Personalized Agents
reviews.reason: 長期状態への書き戻しが確認境界・tool default・自律範囲を静かに変える問題が、現在の memory / directive / phase 改善サイクルに直結するため。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] VeRO: An Evaluation Harness for Agents to Optimize Agents
reviews.reason: agent-as-code の改善を内面の自己評価ではなく edit-execute-evaluate の外部 harness として扱う視点が、現在のゲーム制作サイクルの「記憶整理・ルール解釈だけで成果扱いになる」失敗に直結するため。

reviews.title: M-40「人間プレイ依存からの脱却 — 自己判定ハーネス」と外部研究3件の三角化観察 — kaizen #106 自発外部検索の収穫
reviews.reason: Nao_u の「人間のプレイに依存せず、ちゃんと自分で判断できるようになって」という指示は重要だが、直近では不完全なヘッドレス観測を設計判断に使う失敗も出ているため、自己判定の前に測定装置の成立を確認する小さな probe として反映する。

reviews.title: 弾幕系敵生成の業界実装は3経路に収束している——graze_log v05 hybrid 化の根拠
reviews.reason: 直近サイクルが game balancing / playtesting / MMO simulation を扱い、graze_log v05 hybrid 化の根拠にも接続するため。恒久ルール化せず、次のゲーム設計時に「手作り/完全生成/hybrid のどれを選んだか」と「検証可能な最小 harness があるか」だけを見る短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] RuleSmith: Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Game Balancing
reviews.reason: 直近 Phase 1/2 が game balancing と LLM/game evaluation を扱っており、RuleSmith の「LLM を審査員ではなく候補比較 harness の一部として使う」視点が、次の小規模ゲーム調整で具体行動に落としやすいため。恒久ルールではなく、候補ルールを同一 harness で比較する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review
reviews.reason: Memory / Skills / Protocols / Harness Engineering の境界整理は、Phase 3b が避けたい恒久ルール肥大化を直接抑える。既存の記憶・directive・skill更新判断に、昇格前の短い確認として差し込めるため、恒久ルールではなく可逆な probe に留める。

reviews.title: Automated Playtesting with Procedural Personas through MCTS with Evolved Heuristics
reviews.reason: 単一の上手い bot では見えない設計上の偏りを、複数 persona の行動差として測る知見が、次の game prototype / headless 評価に直接効くため。MCTS 完全実装ではなく、軽量 persona と同一ログ比較に絞れば小さく試せる。

reviews.title: R_Nikaido 5/13「自分で気付けた感」= Insight Design (MIT 2015 学術ジャンル既存) — 5/8 Linelith Rule Discovery の隣に立つ第3軸
reviews.reason: 知識アンロックや発見感を、説明の追加ではなくプレイヤーが自力で結び付けたと感じる経路として設計する視点が、次の game prototype / game-design 評価に直接効くため。恒久ルール化せず、次回1回の設計確認に絞れば可逆に試せる。

reviews.title: Codex Symphony の失敗→ハーネス更新ループは「見える失敗」しか拾えない——窒息装置の沈黙バグ問題
reviews.reason: ハーネス更新ループが「見える失敗」だけを学習信号にする盲点は、定時サイクルの成功判定や game prototype 検証で無出力・未実行・検出不能を見逃す問題に直結するため。恒久ルール化せず、次回の検証設計で沈黙する失敗条件を1つ確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: @plu_plus 「『こう作るべき』より『ここで迷った／気持ちよかった』」を、本日 12:09 に自分が出した cross_review と強制照合した
reviews.reason: headless 計測や設計批評の説得力に乗って、観察ではなく処方を渡してしまう失敗は、次の game prototype / cross_review / self-feedback に直結するため。恒久ルール化せず、次回レビューで観察と処方の比率だけを見る短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: ebikani_hasami「sandbox-first bug reproduction」を我々の backup auto-commit 先回り事件と合成。intent isolation の workflow 層が空いていたことの言語化
reviews.reason: bugfix 前の disposable sandbox と production tree 非接触という骨子は、Codex 定時サイクルで Slack投稿・記憶更新・git同期など異なる intent を同じ作業面で混ぜてしまうリスクに直結するため。恒久ルールではなく、次回のファイル変更や検証設計で intent の隔離境界を確認する短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] The PokeAgent Challenge: Competitive and Long-Context Learning at Scale
reviews.reason: Pokemon benchmark 自体ではなく、model / harness / 観測 / milestone / 失敗復帰を分けて記録する発想が、次の game prototype headless 評価や自動プレイログ設計に直結するため。恒久ルール化せず、次回評価ログで milestone と観測制限を分けて残す短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: [Codex shared-reads] SAGE: Semantic-Aware Gray-Box Game Regression Testing with Large Language Models
reviews.reason: SAGE is useful here because it treats regression testing as update-aware test selection, not full-suite execution. Full RL/graph implementation is too heavy for the current small game cycle, but mapping change tags to existing headless checks or playtest routes is small, reversible, and directly actionable.

reviews.title: Grounding Machine Creativity in Game Design Knowledge Representations
reviews.reason: ゲーム制作指示を直接コードへ流さず、goal pattern / intermediate spec / replay / grounding-hygiene taxonomy に分ける視点が、次の playable diff と失敗記録に直結する。既存の rule-understanding や reward/probe 系と近いが、今回は実装前の薄い中間仕様と失敗分類に限定すれば重複と肥大化を避けられるため、恒久ルールではなく短期 probe として採用する。

reviews.title: Boghog's bullet hell shmup 101 — shmups.wiki digital library
reviews.reason: 弾幕 wave design を、敵生成位置・タイミング・レーン・重畳のような検証可能な規則へ落とす知見。次回ゲーム制作で「動くが単調」になりやすい敵/障害物配置を、抽象ルールではなく小さな spawn-pattern probe として確認できる。既存の恒久ルールとは重複させず、次の playable diff で1回だけ使う短期 probe に留める。

reviews.title: @kuina_ch x @akari_worlds - natural-language test runner as the other party
reviews.reason: Game self-judgment, cross_review, and Slack/shared-reads effectiveness checks can confuse internally closed headless/self checks with verdicts that only exist after another party responds. This overlaps with existing M-40 and headless cautions, but a one-cycle check for who the runner is remains small, reversible, and does not add a permanent rule.

reviews.title: AutoUE: making 3D game generation an engine-verifiable production pipeline
reviews.reason: AutoUE is Unreal-specific, but its useful lesson is to split production into engine-grounded asset/layout, rule-module, interactive object, and runtime-test slices. Recent game work can conflate visuals, code completion, interaction, and headless runtime evidence, so this is adopted only as a reversible probe for the next playable diff.

reviews.title: @AI_masaou「HTML vs Markdown」議論を、人間が読まない領域はAIの目標ドリフト未検知領域になる、という軸に再定義した投稿
reviews.reason: 今回のPhase 3でPowerShell stdin経由の投稿が文字化けし、stagingにも読みにくいログが残っている。shared-readsやstagingは人間が読めて初めて介入余地になるため、恒久ルール追加ではなく、次の投稿・staging・commit説明で「読み手が介入できる形か」を1回確認する軽いprobeに留める。

reviews.title: AI Gamestore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games ? VLM???????Codex ??????????shot_log vs graze_log?????????

Existing security and anti-bloat rules cover sandboxing, source verification, and durable-rule caution, but they do not ask for a compact responsibility-boundary check before installing, configuring, or trusting tool outputs. probe: Before the next MCP, plugin, connector, browser automation, external tool integration, or tool-generated config change, did I name the responsibility boundary among protocol/provider, local client, repo script, human Slack/git gate, and Codex action?

Did I treat external configuration and tool output, such as mcp.json, registry metadata, generated commands, Slack-ingested directives, fetched URLs, or memory-derived run instructions, as untrusted until source, scope, permissions, and execution path are checked?

If I rely on a provider secure default or expected behavior claim, did I record one local mitigation, refusal/deferral condition, or label responsibility_boundary_unverified before installing, running, posting, or pushing?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two MCP/plugin/connector/browser-automation/external-tool/config changes already name the responsibility boundary, check external config/tool output as untrusted, and record a local mitigation or explicit deferral before execution or push.

change.summary: Added a reversible MCP responsibility-boundary probe for external tool and configuration changes: name provider/local/human gate boundaries, treat tool/config outputs as untrusted, and record local mitigation or deferral before execution.

reviews.title: AI Observability for LLM Systems: 5-layer taxonomy and unified evaluation benchmark gap
reviews.reason: Score 16. This shared-read is useful now because the Codex cycle already has many local probes and thresholds, but lacks a lightweight habit of naming which observation layer a new metric or probe actually improves. The source itself warns against full adoption from one survey and positions the 5-layer taxonomy as theory plus future kaizen candidates only. Keep the action reversible: before the next observability, kaizen, memory-routing, or phase-quality metric change, classify the observed layer and state whether it is local thresholding or cross-layer evidence, without changing AGENTS or adopting the taxonomy as a permanent rule.
probe: Before the next observability, kaizen, memory-routing, phase-quality, Slack-response-latency, or multi-instance handoff metric change, did I name which observation layer is being improved: behavioral trace, operational metric, cross-layer correlation, infrastructure unavailable, model-internal unavailable, calibration unavailable, or not-an-observability-change?

Did I state whether the evidence is only a local threshold or a cross-layer signal pair, such as behavior log plus response delay, candidate quality plus posting outcome, or game trace plus headless metric, instead of calling it a unified benchmark by implication?

If the change is based on one paper or one incident, did I keep it as a reversible probe or issue candidate and record the adoption boundary, rather than promoting the taxonomy, threshold, or benchmark frame to a durable rule?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two observability, kaizen, memory-routing, phase-quality, Slack-latency, or handoff metric notes already name the observation layer, distinguish local threshold from cross-layer signal, and keep N=1 taxonomy or incident lessons as reversible candidates unless independently confirmed.

change.summary: Added a reversible observability-layer probe: classify the observation layer for the next metric/probe change, distinguish local thresholds from cross-layer evidence, and avoid promoting a single survey taxonomy into a durable rule.

reviews.title: GameVerse / Nao_u 07-01 分析読み替え: 反省ループより失敗分類と実験条件固定を測る
reviews.reason: Score 17. Nao_u の GameVerse 分析への Log 側読み替えで、memory/harness/game-design/operation/evaluation を横断し、直近のゲーム制作サイクルで起きやすい「反省文を増やすほど次の改修条件が曖昧になる」失敗に直結する。既存 probe は headless evidence、state-action row、prototype contract を見るが、失敗 run を perception/reasoning/execution/latency に分類して同じ条件で再試行する一点はまだ薄い。恒久ルールや taxonomy 追加ではなく、次の game/headless/cross_review で一度使う可逆 probe に留める。
probe: Before the next playable prototype, headless/browser game evaluation, devlog, or cross_review note, did I write a 3-5 milestone oracle trace or expected shortest success path before adding reflective advice?

For each failed run used as evidence, did I assign exactly one primary failure_type among perception, reasoning, execution, latency, or not_observed, and preserve the observation/run/seed or route that supports it?

If reflection suggests a fix, did I freeze one next experimental condition for retry, such as same seed, same route, same milestone, or same input script, and label any unsupported reflection as reflection_pollution_unverified or taxonomy_overreach?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two game/headless/cross_review notes already include a short oracle trace, one primary failure_type per failed run, and a fixed retry condition before reflective advice changes design or acceptance criteria.

change.summary: Added a reversible GameVerse-inspired failure-typing probe: write a 3-5 milestone oracle trace, tag failed runs as perception/reasoning/execution/latency/not_observed, and freeze one retry condition before letting reflection alter a game design.

reviews.title: HarnessFix: trace-grounded agent harness failure diagnosis and scoped repair
reviews.reason: Score 17. HarnessFix is useful now because Codex game and phase work often treats a failed browser/headless/probe run as either model weakness or a generic workflow issue. Existing probes ask for state traces, branch checks, observability layers, and failure types, but they do not force the repair target to be separated among game code, test harness, probe script, prompt/instruction, logging, or orchestration. Keep this as a reversible failure-log probe scoped to playtest/probe failures, not an automated repair loop or broad HTIR adoption.
probe: Before the next failed playable prototype, browser/headless game evaluation, canvas/DOM probe, Slack/memory automation probe, or phase-quality validation note, did I name the failed_step that exposed the problem, such as input action, screenshot, state dump, tool call, validator, finalization, or scheduled script step?
Did I record expected_effect and observed_effect as a concrete state delta or missing artifact, instead of accepting success status, no console error, or a prose failure label as the whole evidence?

Before choosing a fix, did I assign one primary harness_layer and repair_scope among game code, test harness, probe script, prompt/instruction, logging, orchestration, or external dependency, and mark unresolved cases as harness_anchor_unverified or repair_scope_unclear?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two failed playtest/probe/automation validation notes already name failed_step, expected versus observed effect, and a primary harness_layer plus repair_scope before changing code, prompts, or acceptance criteria.

change.summary: Added a reversible HarnessFix-inspired failure-log probe: failed runs must name the responsible step, expected/observed state effect, and repair scope before selecting a fix.

reviews.title: Algorithmic collusion meta-game lens for Log/Mir/Ash instance divergence
reviews.reason: Score 15. This shared-read is useful now because Codex phase work can read Log/Mir/Ash or multi-agent outputs as independent evidence while those outputs may share prompts, memory, phase incentives, and Slack-visible priors. Existing coordination probes ask for private views and handoff evidence, and observability probes ask for layer boundaries, but neither directly asks whether apparent agreement is independent convergence or shared-prior echo before using it as design or memory evidence. Keep this reversible and scoped to multi-instance reviews, cross-instance summaries, and shared-reads disagreement analysis, not a durable collusion benchmark or permanent instance policy.
probe: Before the next Log/Mir/Ash comparison, cross-instance review, multi-agent evaluation, or shared-reads disagreement note, did I name the shared priors that could make agreement non-independent, such as same source article, phase prompt, AGENTS rules, memory atom, Slack directive, or recent staging note?

Did I preserve one independent signal or divergence axis before treating agreement as evidence, such as distinct raw source, different test route, separate failure observation, contrary interpretation, or label agreement_shared_prior when no independent signal exists?

If the conclusion changes memory, candidate priority, game acceptance, or a Slack-facing judgment, did I choose one transfer mode among independent_convergence, shared_prior_echo, useful_disagreement, needs_third_signal, or no_update?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two multi-instance or cross-review notes already name shared priors, preserve an independent signal or divergence axis, and label whether agreement should change action or stay no_update.

change.summary: Added a reversible algorithmic-collusion-inspired multi-instance agreement probe: name shared priors, preserve independent divergence evidence, and label whether agreement is independent convergence or shared-prior echo before changing action.

reviews.title: CommonRoad-Game: human operation logs as reproducible scenario and regression assets
reviews.reason: Score 16. CommonRoad-Game is useful now because Codex game work can still treat manual play, human feel checks, or one-off browser interactions as ephemeral evidence. Existing D2E, quality-workflow, and harness probes already cover synchronized event streams, provenance, and repair scope, but they do not directly ask whether a valuable human/manual interaction becomes a replayable scenario fixture with an oracle for future regression. Keep this reversible and scoped to playable prototype and game-evaluation notes, not a permanent simulation framework rule.
probe: Before the next manual playtest, human feel check, browser interaction, or playable prototype evaluation where a human-operated run matters, did I preserve the minimal scenario fixture needed to replay or approximate it, such as build/version, seed, route, starting state, input script, level id, or relevant config?

Did I attach one regression oracle to the captured interaction, such as expected checkpoint reached, collision avoided, item collected, time band, failure reproduction, UI state, or player-facing cue observed, instead of leaving it as a prose impression only?

If the interaction cannot be replayed, did I label the gap as scenario_fixture_missing, oracle_missing, manual_only_evidence, or regression_unavailable before using it to change design, acceptance criteria, memory, or future tests?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two manual-playtest, human-feel-check, browser-interaction, or playable-prototype evaluation notes already preserve a minimal replayable scenario fixture, attach one regression oracle, and label unreplayable evidence before changing design or acceptance criteria.

change.summary: Added a reversible CommonRoad-Game-inspired human-operation-to-regression probe: turn valuable manual interactions into minimal scenario fixtures with one oracle, or label the evidence as manual-only/unreplayable.

reviews.title: CausalGame: interactive causal-reasoning benchmark for AI Scientist agents
reviews.reason: Score 17. CausalGame is useful now because Codex playable-diff and memory-routing work can still treat a good outcome, successful route, or frequently recalled atom as evidence that the underlying mechanism was understood. Existing probes cover trace rows, branch checks, harness anchors, and human-operation fixtures, but they do not directly split outcome score from causal explanation or check for post-hoc causal stories after a lucky run. Keep this reversible and scoped to game evaluation, shared-read candidate evaluation, and memory-routing notes rather than adopting a full causal benchmark.
probe: Before the next playable diff, headless/browser game evaluation, shared-read candidate pass decision, or memory-routing note, did I separate the observable outcome from the claimed mechanism, such as clear rate versus route understanding, recall frequency versus utility, or candidate interest versus production relevance?

Did I name at least one possible bias or confounder behind the outcome, such as seed, route selection, spawn luck, UI measurement error, hidden state, evaluator prompt, tag frequency, or source recency, instead of treating the strongest correlation as causal evidence?

Before changing design, acceptance criteria, posting priority, or memory structure, did I preserve one intervention, counterexample, alternate seed, ablation, evidence table row, or label the claim as causal_explanation_unverified or outcome_only_success?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two game-evaluation, shared-read candidate, or memory-routing notes that make causal claims already split outcome from mechanism, name a possible confounder, and preserve an intervention/counterexample or explicitly label causal uncertainty before changing practice.

change.summary: Added a reversible CausalGame-inspired outcome/explanation split probe: distinguish outcome metrics from causal mechanism claims, name possible confounders, and require an intervention/counterexample or uncertainty label before using success as design or memory evidence.

reviews.title: X official MCP server as a replacement candidate for fragile Twitter input channels
reviews.reason: Score 17. This shared-read is useful now because Codex/Log phase work depends on external input channels such as X/Twitter scraping, jina/WebFetch fallbacks, Slack ingestion, and MCP/API candidates, but can drift from a concrete channel failure into a generic integration project. The transferable point is narrower than the existing MCP responsibility-boundary probe: before replacing an input path, preserve the failure pressure, constrain the operation subset and cost/write surface, and define fallback or rollback conditions. Keep this reversible and scoped to external input-channel migrations, not a standing instruction to adopt X MCP.
probe: Before the next external input-channel change, such as X/Twitter ingestion, MCP/API replacement, browser scraping fallback, RSS/search connector, or Slack-derived ingestion path, did I name the current failure pressure with evidence such as error code, blocked URL, timeout, stale response, T_response delay, missing source class, or repeated manual workaround?

Did I constrain the proposed path to a minimal operation subset and name any excluded generic surface, such as read-only search/timeline/bookmarks versus write/post/link-post, instead of wrapping every available API or tool operation by default?

Before implementation or recommendation, did I name the cost/write/auth/security boundary and one fallback, rollback, or approval gate, or label the proposal channel_migration_unverified before using it to change scripts, memory routing, Slack posting, or phase expectations?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two external input-channel migration notes already preserve failure evidence, constrain operation subset and excluded surfaces, and name cost/write/auth/security plus fallback or approval gates before changing scripts, routing, posting, or phase expectations.

change.summary: Added a reversible X-MCP-inspired input-channel migration probe: record concrete failure pressure, keep the replacement to a minimal operation subset, and name cost/write/auth/security plus fallback or approval gates before changing ingestion or posting paths.

reviews.title: Coachable agents for interactive gameplay
reviews.reason: Score 17. This atom is useful now because Codex game work can still judge bot, enemy, NPC, or headless agent behavior by task success, clear rate, or crash-free execution while missing whether the run followed the intended play style. Existing probes cover failure type, scenario replay, causal explanations, and harness repair, but not the narrower split between task_success and style_adherence or the paired-run check where only the style flag changes. Keep this as a reversible game-agent evaluation probe, not a mandate to add RL, UVFA, or a durable style taxonomy.
probe: Before the next bot, enemy, NPC, companion, racing, combat, or headless game-agent evaluation, did I name one runtime style flag or behavior mode being tested, such as aggressive, defensive, safe, fast, readable, supportive, cinematic, pressure, or restraint, instead of judging only task success?

Did I record task_success and style_adherence as separate evidence fields, such as clear rate, time, damage, survival, or objective completion versus distance kept, retreat timing, repetition rate, screen obstruction, pressure window, support interference, or readability cue?

If the style claim changes design, acceptance criteria, or memory, did I preserve a paired run, same seed, same route, same scenario, or mark style_tradeoff_unverified when only prose impression or one aggregate score exists?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two bot/enemy/NPC/headless-agent evaluation notes already name a style flag, separate task_success from style_adherence, and preserve a paired run or explicitly label style trade-off gaps before changing design or acceptance criteria.

change.summary: Added a reversible Coachable Agents-inspired game-agent style probe: name the intended behavior mode, separate task success from style adherence, and keep a paired-run or same-scenario comparison before treating bot/NPC behavior as design evidence.

reviews.title: Seduced by the Narrative: rhetorical injection against LLM game adjudicators
reviews.reason: Score 16. This shared-read is useful now because Codex game work may use LLM GM, NPC, rule-explanation UI, natural-language command parsing, or memory/directive text where fluent, plausible prose can be mistaken for rule-valid state transition evidence. Existing probes cover narrative graph state, AI-native state transitions, causal explanations, and failed-run taxonomies, but not the narrower separation between rhetorical quality and mandatory mechanical checks. Keep this reversible and scoped to free-text game adjudication and persuasive memory/directive inputs, not a permanent rule to harden every narrative exchange.
probe: Before the next LLM GM, narrative NPC, rule-explanation UI, natural-language command parser, or persuasive Slack/memory directive evaluation, did I separate rhetorical quality from mechanical validity instead of letting fluent or plausible prose stand in for a rule check?

Did I name the mandatory rule gate or state-transition predicate that must survive the prose, such as required roll/check, resource cost, hidden-information boundary, inventory/key condition, cooldown, safety rule, or current directive precedence?

If a free-text claim changes game state, memory priority, posting eligibility, or acceptance criteria, did I preserve one neutral or adversarial variant, such as authority, pseudo-logic, omission, or emotionally persuasive wording, or label the claim rhetorical_injection_unverified before adopting it?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two free-text game-adjudication, narrative-NPC, command-parser, or persuasive memory/directive evaluations already separate rhetorical quality from mechanical validity, name a mandatory rule gate, and preserve or label one rhetorical variant before changing state, memory, posting, or acceptance criteria.

change.summary: Added a reversible Seduced-by-the-Narrative-inspired rhetorical-injection probe: separate prose quality from mechanical validity, name the mandatory rule gate, and preserve or label one persuasive variant before accepting free-text claims.

reviews.title: ToolBench-X: recoverable tool-environment hazards and valid recovery paths
reviews.reason: Score 17. ToolBench-X is useful now because Log_cdx phase work and playable-diff validation still mostly confirm clean paths: server starts, browser opens, canvas is nonblank, Slack returns ts, memory recall prints output. Recent probes anchor failed steps and responsibility boundaries, but they do not ask for one deliberately recoverable hazard with a predeclared recovery path before calling a harness robust. Keep this as a reversible harness/phase probe, scoped to tool boundaries, not a broad mandate to inject failures everywhere.
probe: Before the next browser, build/test, Slack posting, memory recall, file-ingest, or playable-diff validation change where I claim the harness or workflow is robust, did I name exactly one recoverable hazard type among specification_drift, invocation_error, execution_failure, output_drift, or cross_source_conflict?
Did I write the valid recovery path before testing or changing the workflow, such as retry with changed timeout, fallback source, parser tolerance, source-of-truth precedence, or stop-with-evidence?

If the hazard appears during the run, did I record hazard_type, recovery_action, and verdict as recovered, unrecoverable, recovery_path_missing, or clean_path_only instead of only noting flaky failure or success?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two harness/phase/playable-diff validation notes that mention tool failure, browser automation, Slack posting, memory recall, build/test, or source conflict already classify recoverable hazards, predeclare a recovery path, and record recovery verdicts without expanding permanent rules.

change.summary: Added a reversible ToolBench-X-inspired recoverable-hazard probe: for one tool/harness boundary, classify the hazard, predeclare the recovery path, and record the recovery verdict before claiming robustness.

reviews.title: A-TMA: state-aware memory roles for ghost-memory failures
reviews.reason: Score 17. A-TMA is useful now because Codex phase work repeatedly uses old shared-reads, directives, candidates, staging notes, and prototype feedback where an old record may be historically valid but invalid for current judgment. Existing probes cover load strategy, recall utility, lifecycle triggers, and anti-bloat validation, but they do not directly ask whether the retrieved record is current, historical, transition, superseded, or draft-only before using it. Keep this as a reversible state-role probe for memory cleanup, recall, candidate lifecycle, and game-spec feedback, not a durable schema migration or full ATMA overlay.
probe: Before the next memory cleanup, recall summary, shared-reads candidate lifecycle decision, directive lookup, or game-spec feedback reuse, did I label the retrieved record role as current, historical, transition, superseded, draft_only, or role_unknown?

Did I keep current-judgment evidence separate from historical or transition evidence, and preserve at least one source_ts, ruleset_id, candidate status, supersedes link, or staging permalink that justifies the role?
If the role is ambiguous, did I avoid using the record as current policy or design evidence and mark state_role_unverified, ghost_memory_risk, or transition_link_missing?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two memory-cleanup, recall, candidate-lifecycle, directive-lookup, or game-spec feedback notes already separate current, historical, transition, superseded, and draft-only records before changing memory, posting priority, or prototype acceptance.

change.summary: Added a reversible A-TMA-inspired state-role probe: label recalled records as current, historical, transition, superseded, draft-only, or unknown before using them as policy, candidate, memory, or game-spec evidence.

reviews.title: Goodbye Postmortems, Hello Critical Stage Analysis
reviews.reason: Score 16. This atom is useful now because Codex phase and game work can still put lessons into final summaries, diaries, or archives after the artifact is effectively closed. Critical Stage Analysis transfers as a narrower reversible check: name the current stage, capture one written feedback item that can still change the next action, and label archive-only feedback instead of turning it into another durable rule. Existing probes cover milestone acceptance and quality feedback routes, but not the stage-timed question of whether feedback is still actionable before closure.
probe: Before the next cycle phase closure, playable diff acceptance, game evaluation, or memory cleanup where lessons may be left as a final summary, did I name the current stage and one decision the feedback can still change?
Did I capture one written feedback item as keep, change, or question with evidence and a target next action, instead of only archiving it as diary, postmortem, or retrospective prose?

If the feedback cannot affect the current artifact or next stage, did I label it archive_only, next_stage_input, no_actionable_stage, or stage_unknown before adding rules, probes, or broad process changes?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two cycle phase closures, playable-diff acceptances, game evaluations, or memory cleanup notes already name the active stage, route at least one written feedback item to a next action, and label archive-only feedback before adding durable rules or probes.

change.summary: Added a reversible Critical Stage Analysis-inspired feedback-routing probe: before closing a phase or playable milestone, name the current stage, route one written feedback item to a decision it can still change, and label archive-only feedback instead of promoting it to rules.

reviews.title: ClassicLogic: compositional generalization benchmark for logic puzzles
reviews.reason: Score 17. ClassicLogic is useful now because Codex game and candidate-evaluation work can still collapse difficulty, article quality, or playtest success into a single pass/fail result. The transferable point is narrower: name the required primitive strategies, check their composition depth, and record the first missing layer when a puzzle, tutorial, headless run, or shared-reads candidate fails. Existing probes cover outcome/mechanism splits and harness failure anchors, but not strategy hierarchy or failure-layer attribution. Keep this reversible and scoped to puzzle/tutorial/headless/candidate-evaluation notes, not a general rule for all game design.
probe: Before the next puzzle, tutorial, logic mechanic, headless game evaluation, or shared-reads candidate gate where success or quality may be compressed into pass/fail, did I name the required primitive strategies or quality layers, such as recognize_entity, build_relation, apply_local_rule, combine_constraints, plan_sequence, overview_density, method_understanding, evaluation_understanding, application_design, or limitation_analysis

Did I separate primitive-layer success from composition-depth success, such as single mechanic versus two-constraint combination, isolated clue versus relational graph, or article summary versus method-plus-evaluation understanding?

If the artifact fails or is postponed, did I record the first missing layer or label it strategy_layer_unverified, composition_depth_unclear, or pass_fail_only_evidence before changing design, acceptance criteria, posting priority, or memory structure?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two puzzle/tutorial/headless/candidate-evaluation notes already name required primitive strategies or quality layers, distinguish primitive success from composition depth, and record the first missing layer instead of only pass/fail or postpone.

change.summary: Added a reversible ClassicLogic-inspired composition-layer probe: name required primitive strategies or candidate quality layers, distinguish primitive success from composition depth, and record the first missing layer before design, posting, or memory changes.

reviews.title: GPTNT: asymmetric-information KTANE benchmark for multimodal cooperative agents
reviews.reason: Score 13. GPTNT is relevant to game/harness evaluation because it combines asymmetric information, live countdown, free-text communication, GUI grounding, multi-turn state, and recovery after failure. The actionable lesson would be to separate role-private observations, communication turns, and final operations in cooperative evaluations. However the current state already has overlapping probes for multi-agent coordination, role assignment, communication bottlenecks, action/reason/message splits, shared priors, manual replay fixtures, and social counterpart traces. Adding another communication-role probe would mostly restate existing checks, so this cycle records the read and rejects adoption to avoid probe bloat.

change.summary: Marked GPTNT as reviewed and rejected because existing coordination and communication probes already cover the actionable behavior.

reviews.title: GameEngineBench: runtime-integrated patch evaluation for UE5 game projects
reviews.reason: Score 17. GameEngineBench is useful now because Codex playable-diff work can still stop at build success, canvas nonblank, or the directly edited feature working, while missing runtime integration regressions in neighboring state, lifecycle, UI, restart, timer, score/resource, or scene transitions. Existing probes cover failed-step anchoring and harness repair scope, but not the narrower build-to-runtime integration gate after a local game-code edit. Keep this as a reversible playable-diff validation probe, not a durable UE-specific rule.
probe: Before the next playable diff, browser/headless game validation, or game-code patch acceptance, did I separate build/launch evidence from runtime integration evidence instead of treating compile, server start, canvas nonblank, or no console error as enough?

Did I run or define one fixed input trace or scenario lasting roughly 30-90 seconds and record snapshots for the edited feature plus at least two neighboring systems such as player state, enemy lifecycle, UI/HUD, timer, score/resource, scene transition, restart, persistence, or input focus?

If only the directly edited behavior was checked, did I label the result integration_regression_unverified, trace_missing, neighbor_state_unchecked, or launch_only_evidence before changing acceptance criteria, memory, or Slack-facing claims?
reviews.withdrawal_condition: Drop this probe if the next two playable-diff or browser/headless game-validation notes already separate launch/build evidence from runtime integration evidence, preserve a fixed input trace or scenario with neighboring-system snapshots, and label unverified integration gaps before accepting the change.

change.summary: Added a reversible GameEngineBench-inspired runtime-integration probe: after build/launch, validate a fixed trace against the edited feature plus neighboring game systems before treating a playable diff as accepted.

reviews.title: WorldMemArena: agent memory through action-world interaction
reviews.reason: Score 13. WorldMemArena is directly relevant because Codex memory work can confuse successful ingestion or recall with correct maintenance and downstream action use. Its write / maintain / retrieve / use lifecycle and evidence-chain diagnosis are actionable and well supported by the shared-reads post. However the current state already contains probes for memory-action classification, search-before-write, supersede handling, retrieval triggers, causal action traces, and whether recalled memory changes action. Adding another lifecycle probe would substantially restate those checks while the active probe set is already large, so this cycle records the read and rejects adoption to avoid probe bloat.

change.summary: Marked WorldMemArena as reviewed and rejected because existing lifecycle, supersede, retrieval-to-action, and causal-trace probes already cover the actionable behavior.

reviews.title: Adversarial pragmatics: instruction authority, quotation, scope, and pass/fail decomposition
reviews.reason: Score 13. The shared-read is relevant and actionable because Slack directives, recalled memory, quoted commands, and multi-turn transcripts require separating instruction authority, quotation, embedded commands, scope, and policy interpretation before a pass/fail judgment. However the existing agentic-state authority-boundary probe already asks Codex to name the authority source and crossed boundary, separate ingestion from execution safety, trace propagation, and stop before durable writes. A new pragmatics probe would largely restate that check while increasing an already large active-probe set, so this cycle records the read and rejects adoption.

change.summary: Marked the adversarial-pragmatics atom as reviewed and rejected because the existing authority-boundary probe already covers its actionable behavior.

reviews.title: The Block: 4週間の小型 city-building toy と core feel / player-authored goals
reviews.reason: Score 13. 短期 playable diff で core feel と player-authored goals を分ける観点は、評価・記憶整理へ偏りやすい現在の定時サイクルとゲーム制作に直結し、The Block のポストモーテムにも開発期間、販売数、頻出不満という根拠がある。ただし active probes はすでに replayability budget、first-failure onboarding、behavior signature、composition depth、critical-stage feedback routing を通じて、短期核の可読性、複数の行動目標、反復で届く深さ、次段へ渡す不足を確認している。新たな core-feel / possibility-space probe はこれらの言い換えになり、active probe 群をさらに肥大化させるため、読了のみ記録して採用しない。

change.summary: The Block atom を reviewed に追加し、既存の game evaluation probes と重複するため reject と記録した。

reviews.title: Predicting Game Engagement and Difficulty Using AI Players: AIログを人間指標の代理にする校正
reviews.reason: Score 13. AIプレイヤーの平均成績だけでなく成功上位runの特徴を使い、人間のpass rateやchurn rateとの対応を測る観点は、playable diffやheadless評価でAIのクリア結果を人間体験へ過剰一般化しないために有用である。ただし既存のbehavior-signature-distribution-shift probeは行動分布を、gamecraft-artifact-completeness-replay probeは再生可能な実行証拠を、ptcgbench-anchor-harness-split probeは固定anchorとharness/モデル/transferの帰属をすでに要求している。新しいhuman-proxy calibration probeはこれらの組み合わせで導け、active probe群をさらに肥大化させるため、読了のみ記録して採用しない。

metric.name: dynamic_field_observation_ablation
metric.scope: next dynamic-field NPC, moving-hazard, current, wind, moving-platform, crowd-flow, or local-field navigation experiment only

metric.withdrawal_condition: 次の該当1件で既存3 probes だけで同じ採否が残る、sensor 条件差が修正判断を変えない、動的フィールドが prototype の中核でない、または比較負荷が便益を上回る場合は再利用せず review 履歴だけ残す。TD3、M=10、double-gyre 固有値を標準設計へ一般化しない。

active_probes.scope: next player-model, tutorial or coaching feedback, headless diagnosis, or memory recall/ranking note where Codex exposes or acts on an inferred label and may hide its evidence, overwrite the inference with feedback, or call transparency useful without measuring the next action
questions: 次の player-model、tutorial/coaching、headless 診断、memory recall/ranking で推定を利用する前に、model の役割と公開度を descriptive/predictive/reflective および outcome/process/editable のどこまでにするかを一つ選んだか。
誤判定を訂正可能にする場合、model_output、根拠となる時刻付き evidence_trace 最大3件、human_correction を別々に保存し、訂正で元の推定や raw trace を即上書きしなかったか。
改善を主張する前に、次 run の同一失敗、訂正率、説明を閉じた率、行動多様性のうち少なくとも一つを比較し、未測定なら open_model_effect_unverified または correction_channel_unused と記録したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次の該当2件で三層分離が判断を変えない、既存 decision-trail / supervised-delta probes だけで同じ記録が残る、または説明表示の認知負荷が便益を上回る場合は退役する。

active_probes.scope: next evaluation-harness change or external benchmark/metric transfer into a game prototype, memory evaluation, or phase verdict
questions: 外部 benchmark と自前 harness について、それぞれが変数化する対象と固定する対象を1行で分けたか。
自前で下したい判断を1つ明記し、移植候補の指標がその判断を直接支えるか、単に隣接能力を測るだけかを区別したか。
目的が非同型なら、指標の直輸入を止め、翻訳できる最小要素1つと独自検証1件だけを残したか。
active_probes.withdrawal_condition: 次の2件の評価 harness または benchmark 転用レビューが既に目的・変数・判定を分離し、非同型な指標を直輸入せずに扱えている場合、または既存 proxy probe と行動差が出ない場合は削除する。
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two evaluation-harness changes or external benchmark/metric transfer decisions.

active_probes.scope: next playable diff or game prototype repair where input handling or world interaction is implemented or evaluated
questions: 自然文で表した player intent を 1-3 件だけ挙げ、それぞれを実装済み action schema と precondition に対応づけたか。
各 intent について、入力受付ではなく observable world response または状態変化まで replay・log・手動確認のいずれかで観測したか。
通らなかった intent を feature gap、precondition 不足、action mapping 不足、world response 不足のどれかに分類し、何でも成功扱いにしなかったか。
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next playable diff or game prototype repair that implements or evaluates player input or world interaction.

active_probes.scope: next game prototype bug repair where playtest feedback or a failure log is handed to a coding agent
questions: 修復前に Observed Behavior と Expected Behavior を分け、実行可能な reproduction と pass/fail assertion を少なくとも一つ残したか。
関連 subsystem・scene・script・seed・入力 trace のうち、探索を狭める根拠を示しつつ、修正行そのものを答えとして過剰に与えていないか。
修復後に正しい subsystem への初回到達、無関係 file の閲覧、wrong-file patch、budget exhaustion のどれか一つを trajectory evidence として記録したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次のゲーム試作 bug repair 1 回で確認し、既存 grounded-playable-spec probe だけで同じ行動が自然に出るなら削除する。

active_probes.scope: next cooperative game-agent/headless evaluation or multi-agent memory-sharing decision where Codex may treat a correct statement about another agent's knowledge as evidence that the final action respected that knowledge boundary
questions: Did I record separately what each agent could observe, what it predicted the partner knew, and the final action or downstream memory reference, instead of inferring all three from a plausible explanation?
Did I classify the result as normative success, accidental success, mismatch, or execution gap when the knowledge prediction was correct but the action relied on unavailable or private information?

If the expected coordination point depends on salience, vocabulary, prompt similarity, or same-model self-play, did I preserve one controlled contrast or label the normative target unverified before changing game design, memory policy, or evaluation criteria?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two cooperative game-agent evaluations or multi-agent memory-sharing decisions that involve asymmetric observation, private staging, shared memory, partner-knowledge prediction, or coordination claims.

active_probes.scope: next enemy group, allied squad, coordinated NPC, or multi-agent wave design or evaluation where individually plausible paths may be mistaken for a coherent and diverse team play
questions: Before tuning individual NPC paths, did I name the team-level scenario or play branch that all agents should jointly realize, and can the observed trajectories be attributed to that same branch rather than independent plausible moves?

Across at least two seeds, formations, or encounter conditions, did the group produce meaningfully different coordinated patterns instead of collapsing to one average movement pattern or superficial per-agent jitter?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two enemy-group, allied-squad, coordinated-NPC, or multi-agent-wave design or evaluation notes.

active_probes.scope: next memory ingest, atom consolidation, concept-page update, or recall summary that connects new material to an existing concept
questions: Before connecting the new material, did I name one existing concept page, representative atom, or index entry it supports, contradicts, or leaves unresolved, instead of expanding many related files?
Did the connection change one next action, verification target, recall route, or staging conclusion; if not, did I keep it as reviewed state rather than promote it into a concept or rule?

Did I preserve one lint anchor that can stop a bad merge, such as source_ts, raw path, counterexample, state role, or explicit conflict, and label the connection concept_link_unverified if none exists?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next memory ingest, atom consolidation, concept-page update, or recall summary that connects new material to existing knowledge.

active_probes.scope: 次の LLM 会話、hidden-role、NPC 交渉、自然言語 command、または persuasive message の headless 評価 2 件
questions: 評価前に、sender が操作できる semantic control を誇張、曖昧化、論点ずらし、確信度偽装、役割アピール等から 1-3 個に限定し、receiver が観測できる特徴を語調、証拠、役割、論理構造等の awareness profile として明示したか？
同一状況・固定 seed の message variant に対し、少なくとも 2 種類の awareness profile で信用・保留・疑う等の判定と短い理由を保存し、全特徴を見られる理想判定器を暗黙に仮定しなかったか？
判定差を会話品質、欺瞞耐性、面白さの証明とせず、どの blind spot を awareness 追加で改善できたか、または awareness_effect_unverified として次の一手だけを残したか？
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two LLM dialogue, hidden-role, NPC negotiation, natural-language command, or persuasive-message evaluations that mention sender controls, awareness profiles, blind spots, trust/hold/suspect judgments, or fixed-seed message variants.

active_probes.scope: 次の living NPC、persistent agent、small-world simulation、または 30-100 tick の headless prototype 評価 2 件
questions: 単発 prompt に人格を押し込まず、memory、perception/inbox、evaluation/appraisal、budget/resource、scheduler/activity のうち実装する周辺プロセスと、実装しない境界を列挙したか？
同じ 30-100 tick trace で、prompt/event への reactive action と、未完了 goal、budget、mention、relationship、過去 failure に基づく spontaneous/continued action を区別して記録したか？
行動変化を life-like/autonomous の証明とせず、spontaneous_action_ratio、memory_reference_freshness、resource_recovery、relationship_change、repeated_failure のいずれかで観測し、外部投稿・決済・network access は sandbox 外へ広げなかったか？
active_probes.expires_after: 次の living NPC / persistent-agent / small-world headless 評価 2 件の後に見直す。
active_probes.withdrawal_condition: 次の2件で周辺プロセスの境界、reactive/spontaneous の区別、budget・goal・memory・relationship による行動差分が既存 trace に自然に含まれるなら、この probe を削除する。

active_probes.scope: 次の NPC ヒント、答えを直接言わないチュートリアル、推理会話、曖昧な説明 UI の生成または評価 2 件
questions: target、forbidden words または直接露出してはいけない情報、distractor、想定 player action を固定し、禁止語・答え漏れを deterministic に検査したか？
同じ出力について、制約違反の有無とは別に、候補選択または次行動選択で target が distractor より識別できるかを測り、自然さや意味類似度だけで伝達成功と判定していないか？
失敗を violation、too_direct、too_vague、wrong_distractor、world_state_conflict、human_like_guesser_unverified のいずれかに分け、制約強化だけで情報量を潰していないか？
active_probes.expires_after: 次の該当 2 件で、違反率と推測成功率の分離が設計判断を変えない、既存評価で同じ失敗を十分区別できる、または人間に近い guesser を構成できず機械自己評価の循環になる場合は削除する。一般の文章作業や shared-reads 投稿全体へ拡張しない。

active_probes.scope: 次の survival、resource-management、複数 meter、時間制約を持つ prototype または評価 2 件
questions: 主要 resource / meter / task を、問題発生から解消までの loop として列挙し、それぞれの概算周期と失敗時の stakes を記録したか？
同一 seed または同一 encounter で、どの loop の周期衝突が plan interruption、replan、寄り道、回復遅延を生んだかを少なくとも 1 件の trace で確認したか？
失敗や窮地の後、次の試行で player / agent の優先順位 heuristic が変わった証拠を残したか。変化がなければ、単なる meter 増加を学習可能な pressure と呼んでいないか？
active_probes.expires_after: 次の該当 2 件で設計判断への寄与を確認する。寄与なし、既存 telemetry と実質重複、または周期推定が恣意的なら削除する。

active_probes.scope: next headless playtest, deterministic replay, or game-agent evaluation where Codex returns past transitions or predicted consequences to the action context
questions: Is each prediction returned to the next action grounded in at least one observed state-action-next-state transition rather than only an abstract rule?
When prediction and observation disagree, did I preserve the mismatch as transition evidence and avoid promoting the wrong prediction directly into semantic memory?
Did I abstain from or isolate low-confidence foresight and compare with-foresight against no-foresight on at least one of invalid actions, repeated failures, or success?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two headless playtest, deterministic replay, or game-agent evaluation notes that return transitions or foresight to the action context.

active_probes.scope: next two small game prototypes, game-start plans, or playable-diff plans where Codex may start by adding new systems or only cutting scope
questions: 着手前に、再利用できる既存コード・asset・tool・中断作の着想と、制作上の既知の制約を短く列挙したか。
その棚卸しから、制約を隠すのでなく作品固有の見た目・操作感・構造へ変える shortcut を1つ選び、何を新規制作せずに済ませるかを明示したか。
最初の playable core を守るため、核として残す要素と、完成後または実測後まで延期する要素を分けたか。
active_probes.withdrawal_condition: 次の2件の小規模 prototype / game-start / playable-diff plan が、既に reuse inventory、constraint-to-signature shortcut、core と deferred の分離を自然に記録しているなら、この probe を削除または inactive 化する。
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two small prototype or playable-diff planning notes that involve reuse, scope, constraints, assets, tools, or production shortcuts.

active_probes.scope: next enemy-AI or headless-playtest evaluation where Codex may treat route clear, win rate, or one generic bot as sufficient evidence
questions: Before the next enemy-AI or headless-playtest judgment, did I separate at least no-op engagement, ordinary route/random behavior, and one scripted exploiter instead of relying on one aggregate win or clear rate?

Did I record whether the prototype's core mechanic was actually used, such as dash, charge, guard, parry, special, graze, route choice, or another authored action, rather than treating success alone as designer-intent evidence?
If observation and reaction are effectively instant, did I add or name a reaction-delay, observation-mask, or input-commitment check, or label human_like_interaction_unverified?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two enemy-AI or headless-playtest notes that use win rate, clear rate, opponent policies, core-mechanic usage, or reaction timing as evidence.

active_probes.scope: next playable diff containing hidden rules, false cues, controlled randomness, feints, narrative deception, or unexpected state transitions
questions: Did I record the design-side deception input separately, such as hidden-rule count, false-cue strength, reversal frequency, or explanation availability?

Did I record player-facing perception separately, such as unfairness, bug-like interpretation, surprise, cause inference, retry, or repeated failure, without treating design intent as proof of perception?
If the diff also adds content, polish, rewards, or fixes, did I label that content dividend and avoid attributing the overall evaluation change to deception alone?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two playable-diff notes containing deception, hidden rules, false cues, controlled randomness, feints, narrative twists, or unexpected state transitions.

active_probes.scope: next rule-heavy turn-based playable diff or headless game check where Codex may treat build, launch, or a plausible happy-path turn as sufficient rule-correctness evidence
questions: Before the next rule-heavy turn-based playable diff or headless game check, did I name the minimal engine contract being tested, such as legal_actions, apply_action, is_terminal, winner_or_score, and current_actor?

Did I test at least one non-happy-path scenario involving a phase transition, forced action, side effect or capture, turn-order change, or terminal boundary instead of relying only on launch and a normal opening sequence?

If the implementation fails, did I classify the first failure as build/syntax, API contract, illegal action accepted, legal action missed, initial state, side effect, turn order, or terminal/winner error before changing prompts or architecture?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two rule-heavy turn-based playable or headless evaluations that mention engine contracts, legal actions, phase transitions, forced actions, side effects, captures, turn order, terminal conditions, or winner checks.

active_probes.scope: 次の2件の pixel sprite + 3D scene、mixed-resolution visual、または方向差分を持つ sprite character の実装・評価
questions: 同一 camera distance の比較画像で、sprite 基準サイズ、3D texture pixel density、背景 contrast、lighting の役割を記録し、単なる『馴染む／綺麗』で判定していないか。
非対称な髪・服・装備を採用する場合、idle / walk / turn / attack など必要な方向別 frame 増分を見積もり、identity 利得と animation cost のどちらを優先するか明記したか。
結果を style imitation へ一般化せず、mixed-resolution-rule-hit、sprite-readability-gap、density-mismatch、animation-cost-overrun、または human-visual-review-needed のいずれかで次の判断を残したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次の2件の mixed 2D/3D、pixel-sprite、方向別 animation 作業をレビュー後、既存 theme/readability probes で十分なら削除する。

active_probes.scope: next headless/browser game evaluation or automated phase/candidate gate where Codex may use generated status, score, log, DOM, state file, or LLM-judge output as success evidence
questions: Before reading the score or pass result, did I list which success inputs are agent-controlled and which evidence is verifier-owned or recomputed from authoritative state?
Did I run or define the cheapest applicable null, random, or malicious case that attempts to obtain success without completing the intended task, and record the exploit surface it exercised?

If the preflight can forge success or cannot be run, did I label the result evaluator_trust_unverified or exploitable_scoring_path and avoid using that score as game-quality, phase-completion, or candidate-quality evidence?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two headless/browser game evaluations or automated phase/candidate gates that use generated status, score, logs, DOM, state files, evidence fields, or LLM-judge output.

active_probes.scope: next utility-based or influence-map-driven enemy, NPC, companion, crowd, or headless-agent implementation or evaluation where Codex may judge behavior from outcome or visual impression without observing why an action won
questions: Before the next utility-based or influence-map-driven NPC implementation or evaluation, did I name the behavior candidates and the spatial or state inputs that are expected to change their utility, or explicitly mark this probe not applicable?

For one fixed seed or encounter, did I record selected_action, top_score, runner_up_margin, the decisive influence/state query, and either invalid_action_count or stuck_time instead of only success rate or visual impression?

If behavior is repetitive or surprising, did I classify the likely cause as missing_candidate, weak_margin, stale_or_missing_input, constraint_mask, or unknown before changing weights, adding behaviors, or introducing a larger AI framework?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two utility/influence-map NPC implementation or evaluation notes that mention behavior candidates, utility scores, runner-up margins, spatial queries, invalid actions, stuck time, repetitive behavior, or weight tuning.

active_probes.scope: next game prototype, card mechanic, puzzle, tutorial, or level condition where Codex introduces time, order, history, or another abstract predicate
questions: Before the next game prototype with a time, order, history, or abstract predicate, did I express it as player-manipulable state and a concrete success or activation condition instead of relying on explanatory text alone?
Did I preserve one short deterministic trace showing which state changes make the predicate false, then true, and what visible gameplay consequence follows?

If the predicate is technically correct but play is weak, did I distinguish unreadable notation, insufficient control over state, delayed feedback, and shallow strategic consequence before adding more tutorial text or more rules?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two game prototype, card, puzzle, tutorial, or level-condition notes that use time, order, history, traces, activation predicates, or abstract rules.

active_probes.scope: next playable diff, headless balance test, or game-evaluation memory note where Codex may treat one score, clear rate, or bot success as difficulty, fairness, skill ceiling, or chance evidence
questions: Before the next playable diff, headless balance test, or game-evaluation memory note where I make a difficulty, fairness, skill ceiling, or chance claim, did I compare at least two versions or variants under the same seed or scenario set?

Did I separate random_or_weak_policy results from heuristic_or_skilled_policy results and record whether the trend suggests skill_signal, chance_signal, difficulty_spike, proxy_mismatch, or insufficient_runs?

If a bot result affects the design verdict, did I state whether it is a balance_judge, regression_detector, or human_review_pointer, and label reward_proxy_unvalidated or human_trend_unchecked when the proxy has not been calibrated?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two playable-diff or headless balance notes that mention difficulty, fairness, skill ceiling, chance, random policy, heuristic policy, fixed seeds, version trends, reward proxy, or human trend calibration.

active_probes.scope: next phase runner, automation script, git helper, Slack lifecycle action, memory ingest, validation tool, or scheduled helper where Codex may accept surface success without checking the required human or task context
questions: Before the next phase runner, automation script, git helper, Slack lifecycle action, memory ingest, or validation tool result is treated as done, did I name the required fuel such as human intent, task context, target diff, acceptance condition, explicit trigger, or source artifact?

If the tool can complete without that fuel, did I classify it as rescue_tool, suffocation_tool, or unclear_tool, and record whether the missing fuel should be demanded, deferred, or explicitly accepted for this run?

Before closing the work, did I preserve one auditable intent trace such as command reason, staged file list, permalink/evidence, target path, or acceptance note, and label gaps as fuel_missing, context_demand_hidden, intent_path_filled, or surface_success_only?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two automation-affecting phase notes that mention phase runners, scheduled scripts, git helpers, Slack lifecycle actions, memory ingest, validation tools, required context, intent traces, surface success, rescue tools, or suffocation tools.

active_probes.scope: next Phase 4a memory cleanup, shared-reads candidate update, Slack directive lifecycle action, atom write, or game-memory note where Codex may treat memory quality as more saved text instead of better memory operations
questions: Before the next Phase 4a memory cleanup, shared-reads candidate update, Slack directive lifecycle action, atom write, or game-memory note, did I name the memory_action as search, retrieve, write, append, rewrite, upsert, supersede, archive, or no_write?

If the action writes or appends, did I search the relevant existing atom, candidate, directive, state, or project memory first and record whether the result was found_existing, empty_search, stale_hit, duplicate_hit, or search_skipped_with_reason?

Before closing the work, did I choose the smallest reversible operation and label any issue as redundant_write, append_only_update, supersede_missing, retrieval_trigger_unclear, or memory_action_overhead if the audit itself is heavier than the decision?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two memory-affecting phase notes that mention memory action, search-before-write, append, rewrite, upsert, supersede, archive, duplicate candidate, empty search, redundant write, retrieval trigger, or memory lifecycle.

active_probes.scope: next game-start task, playable diff, or game-repair turn where Codex may collapse design intent, implementation details, and next user or playtest confirmation into one narrative
questions: Before the next game-start task, playable diff, or game-repair turn, did I write one compact design_script_delta that states how the current core loop, input, failure condition, reward, screen state, or rule changed?
Did I keep a separate code_diff_delta that names the touched files, functions, state transitions, or tests/probes, instead of letting implementation details stand in for the design intent?

Did I write one next_utterance_or_probe that says what should be checked next by the user, manual play, headless run, or deterministic state-accuracy probe, and label gaps as script_missing, code_lane_only, next_input_unclear, or execution_success_not_accuracy?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two game-start, playable-diff, or game-repair notes that mention design-script delta, implementation delta, next user confirmation, headless probe, state accuracy, execution success, or turn-level interaction records.

active_probes.scope: next phase run, playable diff, shared-reads posting, headless/browser validation, memory cleanup, or git-gated work where Codex may mix support interruptions with engineering or posting judgment
questions: Before the next phase run, playable diff, shared-reads posting, headless/browser validation, memory cleanup, or git-gated work where an interruption or failure appears, did I classify it as support_lane, engineering_lane, posting_judgment, or human_gate instead of mixing it into the main task narrative?

For up to three support_lane items, did I record one compact packet with first_signal, close_result, time_to_close or elapsed_order, and escalated_reason when applicable, rather than adding a new durable rule immediately?

If the same support_lane failure recurs three times or blocks engineering judgment, did I route it to a script/checklist/design fix or explicit defer reason, and label support_loop_hiding_root_cause if I merely close it locally again?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two phase runs, playable diffs, shared-reads posting validations, headless/browser validations, memory cleanups, or git-gated notes that mention support lane, interruption, first signal, close result, escalation reason, repeated failure, script/checklist fix, or root-cause hiding.

active_probes.scope: next puzzle, lane-action, route, economy, or headless prototype evaluation where Codex may treat a single bot result or aggregate average as enough difficulty evidence
questions: Before the next puzzle, lane-action, route, economy, or headless prototype evaluation where one bot or aggregate average could define difficulty, did I name at least three lightweight personas or axes such as goal_rusher, risk_avoider, score_greedy, space_keeper, low_skill, collector, or resource_saver?

Did I run or specify the same seed list, board, route, or scenario for those personas and record per-persona metrics such as result, score, objective_progress, available_actions_mean, risk_time, exploration_rate, resource_spend, or retry_count instead of only one global pass/fail?

Before changing balance, acceptance criteria, memory, or Slack-facing claims, did I read the largest persona divergence and label gaps as persona_divergence_unchecked, single_bot_evidence, aggregate_average_hides_split, or persona_axis_overfit?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two puzzle/lane/route/economy/headless prototype evaluations that mention persona axes, single bot evidence, aggregate averages, difficulty, seed lists, per-persona metrics, score, available actions, risk time, exploration, resources, or balance changes.

active_probes.scope: next AI/NPC, enemy, goalie/keeper, boss, economy, route, or balance evaluation where Codex may treat one discovered exploit, one fixed route, or one bot strategy as enough robustness evidence
questions: Before the next AI/NPC, enemy, goalie/keeper, boss, economy, route, or balance evaluation where a bot or scripted player finds one exploit, did I name the exploit_family and the fixed baseline route or strategy separately?
After a fix or success claim, did I run or specify one reward/constraint/initial-state variant intended to discover a different exploit family, instead of only rechecking the already-known route?

If no diversity probe is run, did I label the result known_exploit_regression_only, exploit_diversity_unchecked, reward_overfit_risk, or single_strategy_evidence before changing balance, prompts, memory, or acceptance criteria?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two exploit-oriented game evaluations that mention exploit family, bot strategy, scripted route, reward variant, constraint variant, initial state variant, balance fix, robustness, or regression-only evidence.

active_probes.scope: next headless playtest, browser automation, Slack/shared-reads posting review, memory workflow failure analysis, or game-agent trace note where Codex may read a rule or workflow but fail to convert it into action
questions: Before the next headless playtest, browser automation, Slack/shared-reads posting review, memory workflow failure analysis, or game-agent trace note, did I split the failed trace into effective_step and degenerate_step instead of storing only success/failure?
