Did I test the word first in recall or staging output and record one concrete decision it changed, such as deprioritize, verify-before-use, link-as-conflict, keep-as-hypothesis, or promote-to-action, before making it a persistent field?
If no concrete decision changes, did I keep the idea as local vocabulary and avoid adding schema, index, directive, or AGENTS/phase-prompt text?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two memory schema, recall-output, atom/index-field, or memory_redesign notes that propose candidate judgment vocabulary, new fields, index metadata, directives, or phase-prompt text.

active_probes.scope: next memory/state structure change, recall-index edit, atom promotion, compression note, or memory-tree consolidation step where Codex may improve memory without naming temporal scope, representation, and control policy
questions: Before the next memory/state structure change, recall-index edit, atom promotion, compression note, or memory-tree consolidation step, did I name the memory unit on three axes: temporal scope, representational substrate, and control policy?

If I propose a new field, index, directive, or lifecycle change, did I state whether it changes what is stored, how it is represented, or when it is written/read/merged/forgotten, instead of treating all memory improvement as one action?
Did I keep this as descriptive structure first and avoid adding automation, thresholds, or persistent rules unless a concrete failure trace requires them?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two memory/state structure or recall-index notes that change fields, indices, directives, compression, promotion, or lifecycle behavior.

active_probes.scope: next level, map, route, mission, puzzle, resource-placement, or traversal-generation task where Codex may treat one start-to-goal path as proof that generated content is playable
questions: Before the next level, map, route, mission, puzzle, resource-placement, or traversal-generation task, did I check more than one start-to-goal solution path and name at least one reachable mid-state or off-path state that must still be recoverable?

If a route succeeds, did I avoid calling the content safe until I considered softlock risks from optional branches, one-way movement, consumable resources, timing windows, enemy/object state changes, or player deviation from the intended path?

If recoverability is uncertain, did I keep the result as a candidate and name the smallest deterministic check, scripted detour, reachability query, or manual trace needed before promoting it as playable content?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two level/map/route/mission/puzzle or traversal-generation notes that use solvability, reachability, scripted paths, resource placement, one-way movement, or route validation as evidence.

active_probes.scope: next playable-diff review, game-evaluation note, shared-reads candidate gate, or memory-quality claim where Codex may give a broad single-agent review without actively attacking one hidden failure condition
questions: Before the next playable-diff review, game-evaluation note, shared-reads candidate gate, or memory-quality claim, did I name one hidden target or failure condition that should be attacked rather than only summarized?

Did I split the check into attacker, defender, and judge roles for one short round: attacker tries to induce or expose the failure, defender proposes the smallest defense or revision, and judge decides using a concrete log, file diff, route, candidate text, or stated evidence pointer?
If judge evidence is missing or the target is vague, did I keep the result as an open risk or candidate probe instead of claiming the artifact, post, or memory change is better?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two playable-diff, game-evaluation, shared-reads candidate-gate, or memory-quality notes that judge an artifact, post, or memory change.

active_probes.scope: next Phase Game Start, playable diff, game-evaluation note, or prototype repair where Codex may judge game quality using code-like compile/run, screenshot, or headless feedback
questions: Before the next Phase Game Start, playable diff, game-evaluation note, or prototype repair, did I name which feedback loop I am optimizing: compile/runtime correctness, headless regression, visual inspection, route behavior, human play feel, or design hypothesis exposure?
Did I state whether that feedback is immediate and granular or delayed, sparse, subjective, and interaction-dependent before treating it as evidence of game quality?

If only code-like feedback is available, did I limit the claim to implementation readiness or structural regression and name the smallest next play-facing observation needed before calling the game better?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two game-start, playable-diff, or game-evaluation notes that use compile/run, screenshot, headless, route, or human-play evidence.

active_probes.scope: next game tuning note, playable diff, self_judgment table, phase outcome score, or evaluation summary where Codex may add, average, rank, or compare numeric parameters before checking whether the quantity is additive
questions: Before the next game tuning note, playable diff, self_judgment table, or phase outcome score that adds or aggregates numbers, did I label each key quantity as extensive, intensive, ratio, rank, or judgment score?

For any intensive, ratio, rank, or judgment quantity, did I name the composition rule before using it, such as weighted average, max/min, threshold, condition-specific comparison, vector direction, or non-additive qualitative judgment?

Before claiming improvement from a larger total, did I check whether the total only increased an extensive surface measure while the intended intensive player experience, design direction, or evaluation confidence stayed unchanged?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two game-tuning or evaluation notes that aggregate numeric quantities or self-judgment scores.

active_probes.scope: next level, enemy-placement, room-connection, reward-item, or hazard generation/repair pass where Codex may ask one broad generator or one aggregate score to judge the whole playable artifact
questions: Before the next level, enemy-placement, room-connection, reward-item, or hazard generation/repair pass, did I split the change into at most three local editing passes instead of asking one broad generator to optimize the whole map at once?

Did each local pass name the shared deterministic proxy it is allowed to improve, such as unreachable tile count, start-to-goal distance, local enemy-density gradient, recovery-point risk distance, or invisible instant-death placement count?
Before calling the result better, did I check that the proxy is not being treated as fun, tension, or readability itself and name the remaining human/browser/headless evidence needed?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two level-generation or generated-layout repair notes that use local editing passes, deterministic proxies, or generated map quality claims.

active_probes.scope: next Phase 1 external intake, Phase 2 shared-reads analysis, game-design idea note, or memory/action handoff where Codex may preserve a future idea without connecting it to a concrete next action
questions: Before the next Phase 1 external intake, Phase 2 shared-reads analysis, or game-design idea note that preserves a future idea, did I attach it to exactly one target project or phase output instead of leaving it as a general inspiration?
Did I name the minimal next action and evidence pointer for the idea, such as candidate note, staging section, playable diff probe, search keyword experiment, or evaluation fixture?
Did I check whether the idea is advancing the current goal or merely optimizing the intake/search/evaluation machinery, and keep it local or defer it if it risks means-ends reversal?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two Phase 1 or Phase 2 notes that create future-idea seeds or convert external shared-reads into project actions.

active_probes.scope: next game evaluation, playable diff, automated playtest, headless/browser verification, or prototype self-judgment where Codex may treat one run or one route as closed-world pass/fail evidence
questions: Before the next game evaluation, playable diff, automated playtest, or headless/browser verification, did I label each claim's oracle type as binary, statistical, or interpretive instead of forcing every result into pass/fail?

Did I record at least one behavior-characterization note, such as outcome distribution across seeds/routes, repeated failure condition, state cluster before failure, monotony condition, or interesting unexpected behavior?
If only one run or one route exists, did I limit the conclusion to the observed condition and name the next selective exploration condition rather than claiming general quality or coverage?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two game-evaluation or playable-diff notes that use headless, browser, automated playtest, or route evidence.

active_probes.scope: next game evaluation, playable diff, automated playtest, browser/headless verification, or manual-play note where Codex may use one route, trace, or success rate as representative player evidence
questions: Before the next game evaluation, playable diff, automated playtest, or browser/headless verification, did I label each route with the player profile it approximates, such as novice confusion, competent survival, expert optimization, random stress, scripted regression, LLM rule-clarity, or manual feel?
Did I record the movement or input pattern assumptions for that profile instead of treating a single action trace, route, or success rate as representative of human play?

If the build is intended to serve multiple skill levels, did I avoid a global quality verdict until at least one contrast route, seed, scenario, or human observation checks whether the mechanic still works across profiles?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two game-evaluation or playable-diff notes that use automated, scripted, random, LLM, or manual routes as player evidence.

active_probes.scope: next game prototype, template extraction, playable diff, or game_templates_design update where Codex may copy a genre skeleton as fixed content instead of converting it into pressure budget and variation knobs
questions: Before the next game prototype, template extraction, or playable diff, did I express the genre skeleton as pressure budget, role slots, or state-transition constraints instead of a fixed content or placement list?
Did I name at least one invariant that must survive variation and one knob that may vary with seed, player state, tempo, or difficulty?
If I cannot map the skeleton to pressure budget or variation knobs, did I keep the source as reference material instead of turning it into an implementation rule or template?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two game prototype or template-extraction notes that reuse a genre skeleton, design skeleton, or game template.

active_probes.scope: next playable prototype review, headless trace summary, game-design self-judgment, or completion report that claims tension, frustration, relief, mastery, confusion, rhythm, or player experience quality
questions: For the next playable prototype review or headless trace summary, did I list 3-5 concrete gameplay events before naming any player emotion or experience label?

For each selected event, did I write the appraisal hypothesis as a falsifiable mapping such as threat, agency, relief, loss, surprise, mastery, or confusion, instead of treating it as proven human feeling?
Did I keep the appraisal timeline separate from the final fun or quality verdict, using it only to choose one next design question, contrast run, or manual-play focus?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two playable prototype reviews or headless trace summaries that make player-experience claims.

active_probes.scope: next long Codex cycle log, game bot episode, phase incident, completion report, or agent/bot failure classification where surface success/failure may hide observed belief, expected action, or deviation structure
questions: When reviewing the next long Codex cycle log, game bot episode, phase incident, or completion report, did I name what the actor had observed or could reasonably believe at the key decision point?
Did I state the expected action under the user goal or game objective before labeling the actual action as bug, rule misunderstanding, exploration miss, reward hack, or agent drift?
Did I run a brief verify/refine pass that looks for evidence against the first suspicion, so recalled guardrails do not become automatic over-detection?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next two long-log or game-bot reviews where behavior is classified from trajectory evidence.

active_probes.scope: next memory ingest, consolidation, recall, staging summary, or long-lived memory edit where a memory artifact may be trusted or rewritten without naming the failure stage
questions: For the next memory ingest, consolidation, recall, or staging-summary decision, did I classify the main risk stage as ingestion poisoning or context loss, consolidation semantic drift, or retrieval conflict/hallucination?

Did I preserve one evidence pointer appropriate to that stage, such as raw Slack JSONL/source_ts for ingestion, before/after text or diff for consolidation, or query plus competing atom ids for retrieval?
If the failure stage is unclear, did I keep the change to state/staging or a reversible probe instead of rewriting MEMORY, atoms, directives, or long-lived summaries?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next memory ingest, consolidation, recall, staging summary, or long-lived memory edit that depends on trusting or rewriting memory artifacts.

active_probes.scope: next ADV / mystery / conversation-choice prototype brainstorm, LLM-as-player game concept, or game-memory conversion where an external article may be saved without becoming a reusable design check
questions: Before treating a source as useful memory, did I convert it into one production-time question tied to a concrete stuck point, such as first clue, hint timing, partial credit, search burden, or chapter-end confirmation?
Did I state which forced-judgment burden the design device relaxes: ability, exploration,??, or retry cost, instead of only naming a reference game or article?
If the memory cannot affect the next playable diff or brainstorm decision, did I leave it as a candidate/reference instead of promoting it to a playbook, directive, or broad rule?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next ADV/mystery brainstorm, LLM-as-player concept, or external-article-to-playbook memory conversion.

active_probes.scope: next game/headless evaluation or playable diff where a mechanic, scoring change, or player-facing feedback may be judged only by pass/fail, clearRate, or a single verdict
questions: Before reporting improvement, did I name the answer-check timing: immediate, batched, end-of-run, or human review?

Did I include one near-miss or partial-progress signal instead of collapsing the result to pass/fail, such as N of M goals met, distance to target, wrong-category count, or representative failed policy?
Did I state one anti-bruteforce or anti-overfit boundary so the partial signal cannot be gamed by the evaluation policy alone?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next game/headless evaluation or playable diff that reports a mechanic or scoring change.

active_probes.scope: next playable diff / headless game evaluation / cross_review bug or design-quality judgment where a symptom may be mistaken for a verified finding
questions: Before calling a headless/game-eval finding verified, did I write the minimal reproduction condition: initial state, action sequence, expected result, and observed result?
If only a symptom or anomaly was observed, did I label it as suspected rather than verified and choose the next smallest action to reproduce or falsify it?
Did the log, packet, or staging note preserve enough state/action trace for another agent or Nao_u to replay the finding without relying on my interpretation?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next playable diff, headless game evaluation, or cross_review bug/design-quality judgment.

active_probes.scope: next cycle staging / shared-reads post / memory or game evidence update where output volume may be mistaken for a real change in judgment, implementation, or verification
questions: 今回増えた surface は何か: 投稿、staging、state、atom、ログ、スクリーンショット、表のどれかを1つ名指ししたか。
対応する substrate は何か: 次回の判断、実装ゲート、検証方法、検索語、撤退条件のどれが変わったかを1行で書いたか。
surface だけが増えた場合、恒久ルール追加ではなく、削る・延期する・次の最小確認に閉じる、のどれかを選んだか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に cycle staging、shared-reads 投稿、memory/game evidence 更新のいずれかで成果を報告した 1 回で見直す。

active_probes.scope: next shared-reads self-feedback / memory improvement / probe or directive adoption where a candidate conveniently supports an existing belief or workflow
questions: 採用理由を書く前に、この atom が既存方針を気持ちよく補強しているだけではないかを疑い、反証候補または採用しない理由を1つ置いたか。
反証候補を見てもなお採用する場合、採用先を恒久ルールではなく probe / metric / state のどれに狭めるかを明示したか。
反証で弱くなった場合、無理に統合せず defer / reject として reviewed だけを残す判断を許可したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に shared-reads 自己フィードバック、memory 改善案、または probe/directive 採用判断を1回行った後に見直す。

active_probes.scope: next memory / directive / AGENTS / phase prompt persistent writeback
questions: この差分は、確認を省く条件・Slack/tool/git の既定動作・自律実行範囲のどれかを広げていないか。
core state に相当する AGENTS.md、active directive、phase prompt への変更なら、raw/candidate/probe で済む内容を昇格していないか。
危険度が不明な場合、削除ではなく保留・staging 記録・ユーザー確認に落とせるか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次回 Phase 4c または次の恒久 state 更新 1 回で見直す

active_probes.scope: next game-dev / agent-improvement cycle result judgment

game/* を触った場合、最低 1 つの deterministic 確認と、必要なら stochastic な観察ログを分けて残したか。
記憶整理・Slack投稿・日記だけで終わる場合、それを成果ではなく harness 未達として staging に明記できているか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次回 Phase 4a/4c または次のゲーム制作サイクル 1 回で見直す

active_probes.scope: next game prototype headless/self-judgment use

到達できていない場合、設計を変えるのではなく harness 未達として扱い、観測ログ・到達条件・次の最小修正を分けて残したか。
人間プレイ依存を減らす目的が、未検証の自動測定を権威化する方向へすり替わっていないか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に headless/self-judgment をゲーム設計判断へ使う 1 回で見直す

active_probes.scope: next game prototype / graze_log-style content generation decision
questions: 今回の敵・部屋・イベント生成は、手作り / 完全生成 / hybrid のどれとして扱っているかを 1 行で明示したか。
hybrid を選ぶ場合、prebuilt 側と procedural 側の責務境界を 1 つの具体例で確認したか。
その選択が面白さの仮説だけでなく、最低 1 つの deterministic な観測ログや smoke test に接続しているか。

active_probes.scope: next game prototype balance / parameter tuning decision

LLM や headless bot の判断を面白さの最終判定にせず、到達率、死亡時刻、スコア推移、無操作破綻など同一 harness で測れる量に接続したか。
候補を 2-3 個以上比べる場合、同じ seed 数・同じ評価手順で走らせ、プレイヤーモデル依存の限界を staging に明記したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に game prototype のバランス調整・パラメータ探索を行う 1 回で見直し

active_probes.scope: next memory / directive / skill / protocol promotion decision
questions: この知見は、まだ episodic memory として残す段階か、複数事例を貫く semantic memory として整理する段階か、それとも reusable procedure として skill/protocol に昇格する段階か。
昇格させる場合、根拠は「反復して失敗した/反復して成功した実行証拠」か、それとも読後感だけか。読後感だけなら raw/candidate/probe に留める。
skill/protocol 化する前に、既存の AGENTS.md / active directive / phase prompt と重複せず、1回で戻せる小さな probe で検証できないか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に memory/directive/skill/protocol のいずれかを昇格・恒久化しようとする 1 回で見直す

active_probes.scope: next game prototype headless regression / playtest log design
questions: 単一の最短クリア bot だけでなく、探索型・報酬追求型・危険回避型など 2-4 個の軽量 persona を同じ seed / build で走らせられるか。
各 persona について到達率、死亡地点、収集数、寄り道率、滞在時間のうち最小 2 指標を同一ログ形式で比較できるか。
persona を人間の代替として扱わず、「どの観点で壊れるか」を見る検査レンズとして、盲点と撤退条件を staging に明記したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に game prototype の headless regression または playtest log を設計・変更する 1 回で見直し

active_probes.scope: next game prototype / game-design decision involving tutorials, hints, or knowledge unlocks
questions: プレイヤーに直接説明を足す前に、画面上の挙動・配置・反復で「自分で気付けた」経路を1つ作れるか。
その経路は、ヒントや誘導として露骨に見えず、少なくとも1つの具体的な観察対象と次の行動変化に分解できているか。
到達率が落ちすぎる場合の撤退条件を決め、説明追加ではなく最小の配置・タイミング・フィードバック調整から試す形にしているか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に game prototype のチュートリアル・ヒント・知識アンロックを設計または変更する 1 回で見直す

active_probes.scope: next cycle success judgment / game prototype harness or automated check design
questions: 成果判定が「失敗が出力された時だけ」反応する形になっていないか。無出力・未実行・早期停止・検出不能のどれか1つを欠損条件として明示したか。
成功ログや差分が存在することだけでなく、期待したログ・差分・観測値が存在しない時に気づける確認を1つ入れたか。
ハーネスや自動化を更新する場合、そのハーネス自身が沈黙して見逃す条件と、手動確認へ戻す撤退条件を staging に残したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次回 Phase 4a/4c または次の game prototype harness 設計・変更 1 回で見直し

active_probes.scope: next game prototype cross_review / self-feedback / design critique
questions: レビューや自己フィードバックの冒頭で、数値変更・仕様変更の処方より先に、観測した迷い・手停止・破綻・到達不能を 2-3 件書いたか。
AI 由来で書ける観察と、人間プレイでしか言えない「気持ちよかった」を混同していないか。
処方を書く場合、作者や次担当の判断空間を潰さないように、根拠ログ・代替案・撤退条件のいずれかと接続したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に game prototype の cross_review または自己フィードバックを書く 1 回で見直し

active_probes.scope: next bugfix / memory writeback / Slack posting / git sync workflow that mixes diagnosis, editing, and publication
questions: 本体ファイルを触る前に、今の intent が再現・修正・検証・投稿・同期のどれかを 1 行で分けたか。
再現や実験が必要な場合、production tree や本番 state を直接変えずに disposable なログ・候補・一時ファイルで試せるかを確認したか。
複数 intent を同じ turn で扱う場合、stage するファイル・Slack 更新・git commit の境界を混ぜず、失敗時にどこまで戻せるかを staging か最終報告に残したか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に診断から修正・投稿・git同期までを同じ作業で行う 1 回で見直し

active_probes.scope: next game prototype headless evaluation / automated playtest log design

agent / bot に与えた観測制限、行動空間、補助 tool / memory / feedback の有無を、結果とは別欄で書いたか。
失敗時に、停止地点・action count または経過時間・復帰できたかを記録し、model 能力と harness 設計の混同を避けたか。
active_probes.expires_after: 次に game prototype の headless 評価または自動プレイログを設計・変更する 1 回で見直し

active_probes.scope: next game prototype change / headless regression / Phase 4a verification selection
questions: Before changing a game or designing a verification pass, did I reduce the change to 1-3 affected tags such as movement, collision, enemy_spawn, resource, ui, scoring, or pacing?
Did I map at least one existing headless check, manual route, or playtest log to those tags, so the likely fragile probe runs before broad checking?

active_probes.scope: next game idea selection / prototype start / design critique that moves from multiple ideas to one implementation

active_probes.scope: next game prototype self-judgment / headless result interpretation / design critique
questions: 今回の判定対象を、到達率・死亡時刻・ログ欠損など機械的に判定できる層と、気持ちよさ・納得感・作者意図との整合など厚みが必要な層に分けて書いたか。
機械層の数値を、厚み層の結論にそのまま昇格していないか。昇格する場合、どの基準を自分が持っているからそう読むのかを1行で残したか。
厚み層が未校正なら、断定せずに人間確認・保留・次の観察項目のいずれかへ落としたか。

検索判断に効いた成功語と、外れた語を少なくとも1つずつ staging や作業メモに残し、次回の検索器が学べる形にしたか。
新しい atom/title/tags/staging を書く場合、内容の要約だけでなく「次回この件を引くための結晶化語」を1つ含めたか。

active_probes.scope: next playable diff / headless evaluation / game prototype self-judgment where pass rates, policy tables, screenshots, or benchmark-like scores may be treated as player-facing quality
questions: Before treating a headless or benchmark-like result as improvement, did I label it as lab proxy, human-facing evidence, or real-use evidence?
Did I name one likely gap between the proxy and a human player's experience, such as readability, motivation, timing feel, input burden, or exploitability?
If only lab proxy evidence exists, did I choose the smallest next human-facing observation or explicitly keep the claim limited to technical/diagnostic quality?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next playable diff, headless evaluation, or game prototype self-judgment that uses pass rates, policy tables, screenshots, or benchmark-like scores.

active_probes.scope: next Phase 3b/state update, game/headless evaluation, self_judgment, or review packet where having run a check may be mistaken for having tested the claim
questions: Before saying a check passed, did I name the concrete claim it was meant to falsify?
Did the evidence inspect the behavior or decision quality itself, rather than only the existence of a log, screenshot, score, or checklist row?
If the check was mostly ceremonial, did I narrow the conclusion or choose the smallest follow-up observation that would test the real claim?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next state/staging update, game/headless evaluation, self_judgment, or review packet that reports verification.

active_probes.scope: next playable diff, headless playtest, or game evaluation where a successful route, policy table, score, or clear metric may lock Codex onto one known strategy
questions: Before treating the best current route as the design verdict, did I name one observed but untracked fork: unused mechanic, unvisited state, failed-but-informative action, or reachable unexplored condition?
Did the next run or next note preserve at least one low-visit frontier candidate, instead of only repeating the highest-scoring policy?
If adding a full strategy map would be too heavy, did I keep just one fork candidate with evidence from a trace, screenshot, log row, or review note?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next playable diff, headless playtest, or game evaluation that compares routes, policies, scores, or clear metrics.

active_probes.scope: next LLM player / synthetic user / headless persona evaluation where prototype variants, policies, prompts, or game versions are compared as if only the intervention changed
questions: Before reading a variant or policy difference as an effect, did I name the primary outcome and at least one negative control attribute that should not change across conditions?
Did I check whether the evaluator/player persona drifted between conditions, instead of assuming the same prompt label means the same population?
If drift is plausible and no negative control was measured, did I narrow the claim to an observational signal or choose the smallest follow-up comparison that can expose drift?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next LLM player, synthetic user, or headless persona evaluation that compares variants, policies, prompts, or game versions.

active_probes.scope: next rule/directive/probe/hook proposal where a repeated Codex failure may be handled by adding more text instead of a small deterministic intervention
questions: Before adding a rule or directive, did I confirm the same failure was recorded at least three times in the same observation unit?
Did I write exactly one candidate for catching that failure as a small condition in an existing script, hook, lifecycle check, or tool instead of more advice text?
If code intervention is too heavy, did I avoid permanent expansion and reduce the follow-up to one trace, log, or state field to inspect next time?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next rule, directive, probe, hook proposal, or repeated-failure mitigation.

active_probes.scope: next memory consolidation, shared-reads self-feedback, game lesson translation, or directive/probe proposal where multiple observations may be collapsed into one correct-answer label
questions: Before compressing multiple observations into one rule, label, or verdict, did I preserve the distinct source claims and why they rhyme but are not identical?
Did I name one useful friction, barrier, or unresolved difference that should remain visible instead of being erased by correct-answer phrasing?
If the compression does not change the next action, did I defer it to candidate/state notes instead of adding a directive, AGENTS entry, or broad rule?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next memory consolidation, shared-reads self-feedback, game lesson translation, or rule/probe proposal that combines three or more signals.

active_probes.scope: next STG / bullet hell mechanic design, playable diff, README prior-art note, or self_judgment where an existing mechanic is used as evidence for originality or playability

Did I include one recent or current example, not only the canonical old example, when the genre is still commercially active?
If prior art is only a proxy for playability, did I keep the verdict limited to structural plausibility and name the remaining player-facing check?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next STG or bullet hell mechanic design, prior-art note, playable diff, or self_judgment that uses existing games as evidence.

active_probes.scope: next local LLM / OpenAI-compatible provider / atomic.chat candidate evaluation where memory recall, staging summaries, shared-reads drafts, or Slack preflight checks may be moved off the main external API path

Did I keep the main path as the trusted provider and define the local path as B-side evidence only, with one observable comparison such as adopted reason, handoff density, error class, or downstream rework?
If no local provider is actually available, did I record the missing capability as an environment boundary and avoid adding implementation debt or permanent rules?

active_probes.scope: next memory/MEMORY/atoms/index/session_context update, shared-reads self-feedback, or memory consolidation where existing summaries may be overwritten or repeatedly abstracted

元の Slack ts、atom id、raw path、リンクなど、後で抽象を検証できる一次アンカーを少なくとも1つ残したか。
今回の更新で古い判断を変える場合、何が新証拠で何が再要約による drift かを分け、恒久ルール追加ではなく小さな probe/state に留めたか。

active_probes.scope: next database/API/Slack lifecycle/bulk filesystem/git operation where Codex or a scheduled cycle may delete, close, overwrite, publish, push, or otherwise mutate external or hard-to-reconstruct state
questions: Before the operation, did I name the exact target and blast radius: repository path, table, Slack inbox row, channel message, branch, or generated file set?
Did I confirm a rollback or evidence checkpoint exists, such as git diff/commit hash, backup/export, lifecycle evidence field, dry-run output, or explicit no-rollback note?
If the target or rollback is ambiguous, did I reduce the action to a read-only inspection or a single reversible change instead of proceeding with the destructive step?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next external-state mutation, destructive/bulk operation, Slack lifecycle close, or git push that is initiated by Codex or a scheduled cycle.

active_probes.scope: next memory recall, MEMORY.md/session_context update, atoms/per-file consolidation, or phase staging summary where more memory may be pulled in without naming the operational failure it prevents
questions: Before adding or recalling memory, did I name the concrete work state and the failure this memory is meant to prevent, such as stale fact, wrong identity/context, missing temporal lineage, duplicate candidate, or weak evaluation?
Did I choose the smallest useful memory grain for that state: one atom, one raw Slack anchor, one index entry, or one probe, instead of broad context expansion?
After using the memory, did I record whether it changed the next action, verification target, or staging conclusion; if not, did I leave it as reviewed state rather than promoting it to a new rule?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next memory recall, MEMORY/session_context update, atoms/per-file consolidation, or phase staging summary that uses recalled memory as evidence.

active_probes.scope: next multi-agent handoff, Slack/git/memory lifecycle coordination, shared-reads correction flow, or game prototype with cooperating agents where coordination quality may be left to goodwill or vague agreement

Did I identify the mediator or neutral harness that keeps cooperation stable, such as staging format, lifecycle script, test/check command, review packet, or posting gate?
If the contract or mediator would make the work rigid, did I keep one flexible escape hatch and state what signal permits deviating from the default flow?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next multi-agent handoff, Slack/git/memory lifecycle coordination, shared-reads correction flow, or cooperative-agent game design/evaluation.

active_probes.scope: next code-generation, game/headless evaluation, playable diff verification, or tool-generated behavior check where passing fixed tests may be treated as practical robustness

Did I include one smallest stress condition outside the happy-path test suite, or explicitly label the result as fixed-test pass only?
If adding a tournament or broad benchmark is too heavy, did I preserve one failing or low-confidence scenario as the next evaluation target instead of widening the rule set?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next code-generation check, game/headless evaluation, playable diff verification, or generated-behavior audit that reports fixed tests passing.

active_probes.scope: next STG / bullet hell pattern design, playable diff, headless evaluation, or self_judgment where bullet variety, rhythm, difficulty, or readability is discussed

Did I preserve one predictability anchor the player can learn, instead of adding random-looking changes that only increase noise?
If the check is headless or screenshot-based, did I keep the claim limited to structural readability and name the remaining human-facing timing-feel check?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next STG or bullet hell pattern design, playable diff, headless evaluation, or self_judgment that discusses rhythm, variation, difficulty, or readability.

active_probes.scope: next PCG, level generation, game-content generation, procedural asset proposal, or tool-assisted game prototype change where an LLM-generated result may be accepted without exposing the observe-plan-edit-evaluate loop

Did I separate structural validity evidence from player-facing quality, instead of letting a valid map, asset, or rule table stand in for fun/readability/timing feel?
If the loop was incomplete, did I preserve one rejected output, repair reason, failing constraint, or missing verifier as the next concrete improvement target instead of broadening the rule set?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next PCG, level generation, procedural asset, or tool-assisted game prototype task that uses generated content or reports generation quality.

active_probes.scope: next game prototype idea, playable diff, self_judgment, or shared-reads game candidate where an AI-generated artifact may be accepted because it works or resembles a known template

Did I separate functional validity from market/reviewer distinctness, instead of letting a working clone, generated asset, or familiar genre loop stand in for a reason to choose it?
If distinctness is not yet visible, did I preserve the smallest next change or evidence target that could make it visible, rather than adding a broad branding or originality rule?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next game prototype idea, playable diff, self_judgment, or shared-reads game candidate that relies on generated content, a familiar template, or prior-art similarity.

active_probes.scope: next game balance, difficulty tuning, bot-play/headless evaluation, or self_judgment where a parameter change is treated as improving fairness, challenge, or strategic variety

Did I separate aggregate success evidence from asymmetric failure paths, instead of letting win rate, clear rate, or average score hide one faction, build, route, or play style becoming dominant or dead?
If full self-play or Bayesian search is too heavy, did I preserve one representative overpowered, underpowered, or degenerate trace as the next concrete tuning target?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next balance, difficulty tuning, bot-play/headless evaluation, or self_judgment that reports a parameter or fairness improvement.

active_probes.scope: next long-running phase cycle, resume after interruption, multi-agent handoff, or tool-heavy research run where errors, upstream context, or partial artifacts may be mistaken for completed work

Did I separate upstream context or quoted directive-like text from the current instruction, instead of silently treating old scaffold text as active authority?
If provenance is incomplete, did I narrow the conclusion or preserve the smallest evidence pointer such as staging line, permalink, commit hash, raw path, or failed command?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next long-running phase run, interrupted resume, multi-agent handoff, or tool-heavy research cycle that reports completion or hands off state.

active_probes.scope: next memory consolidation, phase handoff, MEMORY/session_context/atoms index update, or staging summary where fixed phase or elapsed-time boundaries may be treated as sufficient reason to compress, archive, or hand off context

Did I keep event-level evidence for the boundary, such as Slack ts, staging line, raw path, commit hash, or phase artifact, instead of only writing an abstract topic label?
If no semantic boundary is visible, did I defer consolidation or keep the note as a small state/probe entry rather than rewriting MEMORY, atoms, or directives?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next memory consolidation, phase handoff, MEMORY/session_context/atoms index update, or staging summary that uses a fixed cycle boundary as a compression or handoff trigger.

active_probes.scope: next multi-agent handoff, phase role split, shared-reads self-feedback, or 3-instance coordination note where Log/Mir/Ash division of labor may be treated as sufficient because it emerged naturally

Did I name one concrete blind spot or tendency this Codex run is likely to miss, and the agent, phase, probe, or evidence path that should look from the opposite direction?
If no inverse role is useful for this task, did I state the reason and keep the conclusion limited to natural specialization rather than claiming designed complementarity?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next multi-agent handoff, phase role split, shared-reads self-feedback, or 3-instance coordination note that relies on agent specialization.

active_probes.scope: next cycle staging, memory cleanup, shared-reads self-feedback, or game design/evaluation step where many candidates, fixes, probes, or metrics compete for judgment at once

Did I separate quantity overload from quality failure: too many decisions to hold at once versus missing the abstraction that prevents generic AI chat?
If both are present, did I reduce the action to one reversible scaffold, probe, or deferred item instead of adding a broad rule, larger checklist, or all-at-once refactor?

active_probes.scope: next game prototype playable diff, sequel/variant iteration, or feature addition where adding a mechanic, mode, content set, or tuning axis may be treated as improvement

Did I classify the addition as same-vector deepening, adjacent support, separate-axis expansion, or opposite-vector interference instead of relying on feature count or novelty?
If it is separate-axis expansion or interference, did I reduce the action to one reversible test, deferred note, or removal candidate rather than shipping it as an improvement?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next game prototype playable diff, variant iteration, or feature addition where an added mechanic/mode/content/tuning axis is discussed as an improvement.

active_probes.scope: next browser game playable diff, Playwright/in-app browser verification, or self_judgment where a build, screenshot, headless test, or code pass may be treated as evidence that the game is playable

Did I write a small rubric for the intended loop such as start, main input, risk or obstacle, score/state update, win/loss, and restart, instead of relying on a generic smoke test?
If the check is performed by automation or GUI agent, did I keep the verdict limited to interaction-level failure detection and name the remaining human-facing feel check?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next browser game playable diff, browser verification, or self_judgment that claims playable behavior from static or automated evidence.

active_probes.scope: next cycle phase decision, memory/Slack/git operation, shared-reads self-feedback, or game prototype evaluation where Codex may finish with explanation-only judgment instead of an executable or inspectable harness

Is the check the smallest harness that helps the actual judgment, rather than making harness construction the new goal?
If the check cannot be run, did I record the reason and evidence pointer in staging/state instead of adding a permanent rule or large mechanism?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next cycle phase decision, memory/Slack/git operation, shared-reads self-feedback, or game prototype evaluation that reports a judgment without an executable or inspectable check.

active_probes.scope: next repo implementation, code review, memory-system change, phase handoff, or scheduled-cycle fix where a local patch may be mistaken for repository-level understanding

If there is structural dependency, did I run or record one smallest inspectable check such as rg, git diff, an existing test, or state-file inspection?
If the check cannot be done, did I avoid claiming repository-level understanding and leave the unverified boundary plus evidence pointer in staging/state?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next repo implementation, code review, memory-system change, phase handoff, or scheduled-cycle fix that relies on local file evidence.

Did I identify one typed or inspectable contract for that bus, such as required JSON keys, markdown heading, lifecycle field, test output, or schema-like invariant, instead of relying only on implicit script behavior?
Did I name the observation cost or observer worker that will catch drift after the change, and keep it to the smallest existing check rather than adding a broad new framework or permanent rule?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next worker-boundary, phase-system, memory-system, Slack lifecycle, scheduled-cycle, or game-evaluation change that depends on a shared bus artifact.

active_probes.scope: next Slack directive/broadcast lifecycle, memory ingest/recall, atom consolidation, or staging conclusion where a Slack post or atom relation is used as evidence

If entity alias drift affects the judgment, did I name at least one canonical form or alias candidate, and leave an evidence note when identity is ambiguous?
If relation direction or conflicting facts affect lifecycle closing, recall, or staging conclusions, did I preserve both source timestamps and narrow the conclusion instead of overwriting?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next Slack lifecycle, memory ingest/recall, atom consolidation, or staging conclusion that depends on actor, target, relation direction, or conflicting source evidence.

active_probes.scope: next game-agent evaluation, self-play/self-evolution report, LLM-as-player benchmark, or phase/game prototype judgment where improvement may come from model ability, prompt/policy changes, harness scaffolding, or environment constraints

Did I preserve one inspectable turn-level trace, hidden-information constraint, or decision-state example instead of relying only on aggregate win rate, score, or pass/fail?

active_probes.scope: next game prototype, headless playtest, LLM-as-player benchmark, or game-evaluation staging where raw score may hide whether perception, memory, reflection, rule hints, or reasoning budget caused the change

Did I compare at least one same-seed or same-scenario delta between scaffold-off and scaffold-on before claiming the game, agent, prompt, or harness improved?

If a scaffold improves the score, did I narrow the diagnosis to the module it helped, such as UI/state readability, memory of failed moves, planning depth, or timing/action-space limits, instead of treating the score as overall quality?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next game/headless evaluation that uses a scaffold, module toggle, prompt aid, memory aid, structured observation, or reasoning-budget change.

active_probes.scope: next self-improving-agent paper, external research judgment, memory-redesign decision, autonomous-game evaluation, or phase analysis where an improvement may come from harness, weights, memory, or verifier changes
questions: For the next self-improving-agent, external-paper, memory-redesign, or autonomous-game evaluation, did I classify the claimed improvement by axis: harness/prompt/tool logic, weights/model update, memory/retrieval layer, or verifier/evaluation change?
Did I name whether the evidence uses one fixed verifier or a perturbation/cross-verifier check before treating the improvement as robust?
If the result only optimizes a fixed verifier, did I narrow the conclusion to verifier-bound improvement and preserve one memory/evidence hook for future Goodhart or perturbation checks?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next self-improvement, external-paper, memory-redesign, or autonomous-game evaluation that claims an improvement or robustness signal.

active_probes.scope: next memory index line, skill, probe, directive, phase instruction, or recall surface change where adding knowledge may increase routing cost or hide useful body content

Did I name the closest existing probe, skill, directive, or index entry and state whether the change fixes a missing description, non-actionable body content, or an observed routing/recall failure?
If there is no observed routing failure, recall miss, or body-noise problem, did I avoid adding a new mechanism and record the atom as reviewed/deferred or state-only instead?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next memory index, skill, probe, directive, phase instruction, or recall-surface change that adds or restructures routing text.

active_probes.scope: next game template, design skeleton, wave, level, enemy/event budget, or genre-pattern application where a source template may be copied with the wrong unit of measure

Did I map that source unit to the target game's real control unit, such as threat budget per wave, event pressure over time, player-choice slot, mechanic opportunity, or spatial section?
If the unit mapping is weak, did I keep the result reversible as a project note or probe instead of promoting it to a general design rule or R-layer memory?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next game-template, design-skeleton, wave/level budget, or genre-pattern application that borrows structure from another source.

active_probes.scope: next game-template, external benchmark, agent-skill framework, harness, or evaluation-rubric adoption where an outside framework may be copied into Codex/Pot/game work

Did I compare that measured variable with the local target variable, such as playable diff quality, design-hypothesis exposure, headless regression, player-facing loop, or memory/skill routing cost?
If the variables differ, did I keep only the compatible reference piece and record the non-adopted part instead of promoting the whole framework to a rule, template, or evaluation gate?

active_probes.scope: next memory recall/consolidation, phase staging decision, cross_review proposal, game feedback application, or completion report where an older memory or directive becomes a premise for current action

Did I check one later or current signal that could implicitly invalidate it, such as newer staging, active directive status, git state, current game diff, Slack lifecycle state, or a more recent atom?
If the later signal changes the premise, did I update the action or narrow the conclusion instead of carrying the stale premise into a proposal, evaluation, or completion report?
active_probes.expires_after: Review after the next memory, staging, cross_review, game-feedback, or completion-report action that relies on an older premise.

active_probes.scope: next Slack post, cycle staging section, shared-reads analysis, completion report, or self-judgment where adding more explanation may reduce the reader's ability to decide

Did I remove or defer at least one layer of explanation that only proves diligence but does not change that decision?
If detail is necessary, did I put the decision and evidence pointer first, then move extra context to a linked file, candidate note, or later phase item?

active_probes.scope: next multi-agent handoff, phase cross-response, instance-divergence note, Slack coordination reply, or shared-reads self-feedback where similar conclusions may be mistaken for coordination

Did I preserve one delayed-influence evidence pointer, such as source_ts, staging line, quoted prior output, diff, or decision change, showing that one agent output changed another agent or phase decision?
If the evidence only shows common-source alignment or parallel role differentiation, did I narrow the claim to that instead of promoting it to coordination or synergy?

Did I capture an evidence pointer for that case, such as event log, screenshot, video, console output, seed, replay step, or state transition?
If only the normal route was checked, did I narrow the verdict to baseline interaction or smoke-test evidence and leave the off-nominal scenario as the next explicit test target?
